title: Pension peril: is it time to unpick the triple lock? | State pensions | The Guardian
description: Letters: Readers are divided on whether the triple lock should stay or go
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Letters: Readers are divided on whether the triple lock should stay or go
Content: ‘This country can afford to support both its old and young with a decent standard of living.’Photograph: Si Barber/The GuardianView image in fullscreen‘This country can afford to support both its old and young with a decent standard of living.’Photograph: Si Barber/The GuardianState pensionsLettersPension peril: is it time to unpick the triple lock?Readers are divided on whether the triple lock should stay or goWed 16 Sep 2026 12.16 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 12.27 EDTShareThe article about whether the pensions triple lock should be ditched omits several key facts (‘Costing billions’: is the pensions triple lock a lifeline or simply unaffordable?, 12 September). The triple lock was introduced in 2010 to attempt to reinstate the value of the state pension relative to average earnings. The new state pension is just over £12,547 per annum, as your reporter says; older pensioners get a basic £9,615. Both are well below the European average, which is over €16,000 (about £13,800) per year. The UK median wage isabove £39,000a year. Moreover, the age at which the UK state pension becomes payable is among the highest in Europe.The discussion on the affordability of the state pension seems to regard it as expenditure for no return. It is not. Pensioners spend money into their local economy, which generates tax revenues in the form of VAT and income tax from younger people who are dependent on pensioner money for their employment. Better-off pensioners pay income tax in the usual way. In fact, a pensioner with any income at all above the new state pension will pay tax on it as the personal tax free allowance is now £12,570, only £23 above their pension income.The British Chamber of Commerce has called for the triple lock to be scrapped, and the money saved to be put towards tackling the youth unemployment crisis. This is a specious argument, designed to make scrapping the triple lock attractive to young people. This country can afford to support both its old and young with a decent standard of living.Sue HawthorneHaddington, East LothianI think the triple lock should go. It’s done its job and brought the state pension up to a respectable proportion of average earnings and I don’t think it would be right for pensioners’ income to go streaking ahead of everybody else’s (UK retirees with no other income will not pay tax on new £13,000 state pension, No 10 says, 15 September). What’s more, I think pensioners – like me – ought to pay income tax and national insurance, just like working people. Apart from the morality of paying tax, the state is spending at least as much on our welfare as on anybody else’s and it seems only right that we should contribute if we can.Perhaps I’m more fortunate than others. My sole income is the state pension but I travel abroad, I donate to charities, I give decent gifts to the grandchildren and I still end up with a little cash left over at the end of the year. I’m from the generation that was taught how to live frugally yet I enjoy my quality of life: I can buy whatever I want but I probably don’t want to buy that much. I’m content.I know that not every state pensioner can say the same as me. There are too many from all age groups living stressful, impoverished lives which is all the more reason why I ought to pay tax and national insurance if I can. And if I wanted to ask our government for anything in return I would say: spend some of this money on finding me an NHS dentist.Name and address suppliedA more fundamental question about the rates paid for the state pension needs addressing. Having paid in for 46 years, I get a state pension of £241.30 per week. The minimum wage for a 37.5-hour week for an under-18 apprentice is £300. Why does the government, of whatever persuasion, think that pensioners can exist on less than an 18-year-old?Chris MoranStockportYour article about the triple lock is one of many arguing that it costs too much. I wonder how many of those in favour of this do so from the comfort of knowing that they will also enjoy a generous private, or company, pension, on top of their state pension, when they retire. Perhaps they should try living on a state pension – that might cause them to moderate their position very quickly indeed. The photograph you used with your article online, showing three old ladies sunning themselves on deckchairs, may suit the argument to picture retirement as one long holiday, but let me assure you that for many pensioners, it isn’t.Lauren WhiteLincolnThe state pension currently costs about£154bn a year, but what about pension tax relief of about £70bn a year? The bulk of pension tax relief goes to high earners many paying 40% or 45% tax and getting relief at that rate worth on average about£8,750 a yeardespite the fact that very few pensioners pay higher-rate income tax and the average basic rate taxpayer getting about £1,000 a year. Is it perhaps that handing out money to poor or average-income people is a bad thing while tax allowances for the rich is a good thing?John BoxallFrome, SomersetHave an opinion on anything you’ve read in the Guardian today? title: Why I can’t wait to get into a driverless car | Self-driving cars | The Guardian
description: Letters: Lars Janssen says self-driving vehicles would be a boon for him as he has an eye condition and can’t drive, in response to an article by Adrian Chiles. Plus letters from Richard Connell and Michael Fuller
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Letters: Lars Janssen says self-driving vehicles would be a boon for him as he has an eye condition and can’t drive, in response to an article by Adrian Chiles. Plus letters from Richard Connell and Michael Fuller
Content: A Waymo self-driving minicab in training in central London.Photograph: Jonathan Brady/PAView image in fullscreenA Waymo self-driving minicab in training in central London.Photograph: Jonathan Brady/PASelf-driving carsLettersWhy I can’t wait to get into a driverless carLars Janssensays self-driving vehicles would be a boon for him as he has an eye condition and can’t drive, in response to an article by Adrian Chiles. Plus letters fromRichard ConnellandMichael FullerWed 16 Sep 2026 12.16 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 12.27 EDTShareAdrian Chiles (Driverless cars are taking us on a road to nowhere, 10 September) wants to know who asked for driverless cars. I did. I have an eye condition callednystagmusand will never be able to drive unless a “tech-bro willy-waver”, or anyone else, finds a cure. Fortunately, not every driver is as reckless as the ones Chiles despairs of, and the most careful of all may not even be human.Waymo, Google’s sister company,saysits cars have far fewer crashes causing injuries than human drivers. In July, the USInsurance Institute for Highway Safetyfound that its cars had 68% fewer crashes per mile than human drivers.Anyone wanting to take a swipe at tech-bro culture could pick a better target than a product that can save lives and give people like me independence. Chiles says we can’t be friends if driverless cars are near my top 10 wishlist. Well, I can’t wait to get into one.Lars JanssenHaywards Heath, West SussexMy 18-year-old daughter is severely disabled, will never live independently and is entirely reliant on the support of others. To call the development of driverless cars the “willy-waving” of tech bros perhaps comes from a position of being able-bodied.Driverless cars open up my daughter’s world without the risks associated with her vulnerability. Augmented-reality glassestransform disabled people’s lives. An iPad has taught my daughter how to hold her hand still to be able to point.Richard ConnellRichmond, LondonDon’t be too quick to condemn driverless cars. They could be the saviour of country pubs. There are so many wonderful boozers around where I live, but you either have to drive to them and have one pint, which is not really worth the visit, or faff about getting an expensive taxi. Driverless cars? Bring ’em on!Michael FullerAmpthill,BedfordshireHave an opinion on anything you’ve read in the Guardian today? title: The families facing a food crisis in school holidays | Children | The Guardian
description: Letter: Andrew Forsey urges the government to restore the link between free school meals and the holiday activities and food programme
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Letter: Andrew Forsey urges the government to restore the link between free school meals and the holiday activities and food programme
Content: ‘Any gains accruing to their children in term time risk being wiped out by this lack of support in the holidays.’Photograph: Getty/RooM RFView image in fullscreen‘Any gains accruing to their children in term time risk being wiped out by this lack of support in the holidays.’Photograph: Getty/RooM RFChildrenLettersThe families facing a food crisis in school holidaysAndrew Forseyurges the government to restore the link between free school meals and the holiday activities and food programmeWed 16 Sep 2026 12.15 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 12.27 EDTShareThere are 500,000 children growing up in poorer families who are confronted by a similarly cruel cliff edge to the one covered by your article (Chancellor urged to fix £100k childcare ‘cliff edge’ that prompts parents to cut work, 10 September). It is this group of children who, having recently become eligible for means-tested free school meals during term time, are disqualified from accessing the holiday activities and food (HAF) programme. While the government has rightly acknowledged the need for those children to receive extra help during term time, it has somehowreached the decisionthat this need does not extend into the school holidays.HAF is a terrific programme providing nutritious meals, enriching activities and free childcare for many families. Since its introduction, eligibility for it has always been linked to the receipt of free school meals. But the government’s decision to break that link will result in working parents, earning as little as £7,500 a year, being unable to access this vital support. Any gains accruing to their children in term time risk being wiped out by this lack of support in the holidays.There is still time for the budget to restore the link between free school meals and HAF. Failure to do so will lead all too many low-income families towards a cliff edge in next year’s school holidays.Andrew ForseyNational director, Feeding BritainHave an opinion on anything you’ve read in the Guardian today? Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Brief letters: Reflecting on the Thirlwall report | At one’s peak | Leaving the debate | Cut from the same cloth | End of the odyssey | A word’s worth
Content: ‘Babies in neonatal intensive care units are saved by having consultant neonatologists doing rounds twice daily, trained neonatal nurses and appropriately resourced units.’Photograph: AlamyView image in fullscreen‘Babies in neonatal intensive care units are saved by having consultant neonatologists doing rounds twice daily, trained neonatal nurses and appropriately resourced units.’Photograph: AlamyBrief lettersLucy LetbyLettersDoctors, not cameras, save babies in intensive careLucy Letby case | At one’s peak | Leaving the debate | Cut from the same cloth | End of the odyssey | A word’s worthWed 16 Sep 2026 12.15 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 12.27 EDTShareRe the Thirlwall report on the Lucy Letby case (Thirlwall report: what did it say about Lucy Letby case and what does it recommend?, 15 September), babies in neonatal intensive care units are saved by having consultant neonatologists (ie paediatricians who have undergone subspecialist training in neonatal medicine) doing rounds twice daily (in addition to being immediately available), trained neonatal nurses and appropriately resourced units – not by installing cameras on cots and insulin fridges.Dr ChrisFitzpatrickRetired consultant obstetrician; former CEO ofCoombehospital, Dublin, IrelandFollowing the introduction of a competitive element in the nominative determinism debate (Letters, 15 September), I’d like to advise everyone that I am at my peak.Steve MunroSt Osyth, EssexI have found the nominative determinism letters interesting and amusing, but feel that they have gone on long enough. title: De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comeback | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: United scored two early goals but lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup, following up derby defeat and JJ Gabriel’s request to leave
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: United scored two early goals but lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup, following up derby defeat and JJ Gabriel’s request to leave
Content: Maxim De Cuyper scored what proved to be Brighton’s winner three minutes after coming on.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Nigel French/Apl/SportsphotoView image in fullscreenMaxim De Cuyper scored what proved to be Brighton’s winner three minutes after coming on.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Nigel French/Apl/SportsphotoCarabao CupDe Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comebackJamie Jacksonat Old TraffordWed 16 Sep 2026 17.18 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAcross four days Manchester United have lost the 199th derby against Manchester City, were told by JJ Gabrielthat he wants to leave, and now they have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.Capitulating after being 2-0 up may be the pick of these dizzying blows, as the prolonged boos at the final whistle suggested, and doing so ends a proud 50-year record: the last time the same lead at Old Trafford ended in defeat was Tottenham’s 3-2 win in September 1976.Manchester United 2-3 Brighton, Coventry 1-3 Aston Villa and more: Carabao Cup clockwatch – as it happenedRead moreWhen Marcus Rashford skated in with the chance to take the tie to 3-3 late on, there was no surprise he hit Jason Steele rather than the net.Towards the end, Matheus Cunha was thrown on to join Bruno Fernandes, also a late substitute, illustrating how desperate Michael Carrick was. Yet Charalampos Kostoulas went close to scoring a second for Brighton, as United could not find a route to cancelling out Maxim De Cuyper’s 69th-minute strike that proved the winner.After taking only four points from 12 in the league, serious questions will now be asked about where Carrick’s team are heading; they have to beat Fulham on Sunday to start correctinga dismal start to the season. The manager already looks haunted and he talked afterwards of not caring about being under pressure.View image in fullscreenUnited’s evening started brightly enough, with the 19-year-old Shea Lacey scoring on his first start for the club.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersCarrick said the injusticesuffered against City on Sundaywould give his side an edge and Shea Lacey provided one when decorating a full debut with the sweetest of goals. The 19-year-old shimmied in Brighton’s area, beating Jaouen Hadjam before firing beyond a helpless Jason Steele. As impressive here was Benjamin Sesko’s hold-up work in the buildup as this allowed red shirts to flood forward, Youri Tielemans feeding Lacey.This was eight minutes in and less than 120 seconds later Mason Mount doubled United’s advantage. Rashford’s pace and drive took him clear along the left, again inside the area. A trailing Steele boot saved the No 9’s effort but the ball bounced into Mount’s path and he drove home, via the turf, for a first goal since a winat Wolves last December.Lacey’s strike drew a Carrick grin and delight from Mount, and you wondered how Gabriel – earmarked for the squad in this game, with the chance to become United’s youngest player – felt.Brighton had lost only one of their previous five visits here and a flying start to the league campaign has Fabian Hürzeler’s team in fifth. Yetthe 5-0 hammering of Coventryon Sunday already seemed distant as United continued to dominate.View image in fullscreenCharalampos Kostoulas started Brighton’s comeback just before half-time.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAOlivier Boscagli hit a corner straight out, summing up the visitors’ start, before Matt O’Riley forced Ayden Heaven into an error that led to another. This presaged a Seagulls renaissance that featured a lightning Malick Yalcouyé break but, clear in on the debutant Karl Darlow’s goal, the Ivorian spooned wide. The No 35 lacked the sharpness evident in a Rashford nutmeg of Chema Andrés which embarrassed the Brighton man and when Pascal Gross blasted over this was one more chance spurned by Hürzeler’s men.But then came a goal – and real hope – for Brighton. Hadjam’s long left-right diagonal cut United’s rearguard clean out, and the slumbering Heaven allowed Kostoulas to scamper free, the striker beating Darlow through his legs.Carrick, having beaten onlyIpswich in the leagueandSabah in Europeso far this season, needed a win, and as United (not under him) exited at the earliest opportunity in both domestic cups last season, progressing to at least a second tie in one of them would be welcome.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionA wild Tielemans long-range shot that ballooned over failed to restore United’s two-goal lead but at least the home team were tapping the ball about, operating in Brighton territory, moving the visitors around.View image in fullscreenUnited were frustrated by Pascal Gross’s leveller for Brighton, but things were about to get even worse for Michael Carrick’s side.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersA Sesko burst from halfway had the onrushing Steele hacking away just in time. United were in control. But the question was: could they maintain this and register the type of mature, accomplished display that would show an evolution in Carrick’s team? Sesko, in yards of space, dawdling and being dispossessed when a simple ball would have fed Lacey, suggested not.A loose Rashford pass aimed for Sesko hinted at the same. More promising was a pass for Noussair Mazraoui as he drove into the area along the left channel, as was the subsequent corner that created an opening Tielemans narrowly missed.Quick GuideCarabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over BladesShowA 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sentFleetwoodinto the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents,Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw.Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory.Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net.United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide.Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean.Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal.United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked.Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win overWolvesthree minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute.It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.But then calamity. Diogo Dalot’s hoofed clearance failed to find Sesko as Luka Vuskovic headed to Gross; Brighton’s captain made room and netted with ease. Even worse followed. Brighton raided along the right, Kostoulas’s cross pinged off Mazraoui’s backside, and there was De Cuyper to finish.On 72 minutes Carrick played his ace, introducing Fernandes for Mount, then followed up with Cunha. But United remained toothless.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupManchester UnitedBrighton & Hove Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of club | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The club’s American chair left the club after the deal was secured and said: ‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The club’s American chair left the club after the deal was secured and said: ‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’
Content: ‘It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club,’ said Todd Boehly.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersView image in fullscreen‘It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club,’ said Todd Boehly.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersChelseaBoehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of clubAmerican chair Boehly leaves role after deal is secured‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’Press AssociationWed 16 Sep 2026 19.28 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 19.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTodd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes inChelseain a deal under which Clearlake Capital takes full control of the Premier League club.The American billionaire businessmen Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in a sale mandated by the UK government in May 2022. The private equity company Clearlake had previously owned 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjörg Wyss.Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark WalterRead moreA statement issued late on Wednesday night read: “Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, LP will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.“As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club.”Chelsea said Boehly, the chair, had shown “unwavering commitment” to the ownership group’s belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club. “The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success,” the statement added.“Under their joint ownership, substantial investment has been made across the men’s and women’s senior and youth squads, Chelsea’s training facilities at Cobham, medical and player-support resources, academy development and pathways, and the sporting and business leadership of the club.“Todd Boehly now leaves his role as chairman with Chelsea well positioned for the next phase of development. Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together.”View image in fullscreenXabi Alonso has been tasked with reviving Chelsea’s fortunes.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APBoehly said: “It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”Behdad Eghbali and José Feliciano, cofounders of Clearlake Capital, said: “Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.“Clearlake has served as Chelsea’s majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club’s infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club’s supporters.”Chelsea, who appointed Xabi Alonso as manager in the summer and are sixth in the Premier League, say there will be no changes to day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club.Explore more on these topicsChelseanewsShareReuse this content

title: Enzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZ | Europa League | The Guardian
description: Four days after having a penalty saved against Arsenal, Enzo Le Fée scored from 12 yards as Sunderland won 1-0 against AZ in their Europa League opener
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Four days after having a penalty saved against Arsenal, Enzo Le Fée scored from 12 yards as Sunderland won 1-0 against AZ in their Europa League opener
Content: Enzo Le Fée punches the air after scoring the only goal of the game from 12 yards.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenEnzo Le Fée punches the air after scoring the only goal of the game from 12 yards.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersEuropa LeagueEnzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZLouise Taylorat the Stadium of LightWed 16 Sep 2026 17.06 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGranit Xhaka, Sunderland’s captain, believes it is not unrealistic to dream about Régis Le Bris’s side travelling all the way to theEuropa Leaguefinal next spring.It is rarely a good idea to dismiss Xhaka but reaching that showpiece in Frankfurt will necessitate considerably more efficient finishing on his team’s part than proved evident on a highly evocative night on Wearside.Sunderland 1-0 AZ, Milan 0-2 Benfica and more: Europa League clockwatch – liveRead moreThanks to a second-half penalty from the indefatigable Enzo Le Fée – appropriately the game’s outstanding player – the game ended happily forSunderlandas the home side launched their big return to Europe with a morale-boosting win.Along the way they missed a litany of chances but, in Le Fée, possessed both a high-calibre attacking playmaker and a tireless off‑the‑ball warrior who, time after time, regained possession for his team.When Le Bris was invited later to agree that a player he first coached as a 12-year-old in Lorient’s academy was Champions League class, the Sunderland manager’s smile lit up the room. “Enzo’s a great player,” he said. “I trust him and his quality. I’m proud and pleased for the players and the fans, AZ are a really good side but we played with heart and togetherness.”Occupants of the VIP seats included Jimmy Montgomery, the now 82-year-old hero of Sunderland’s 1973 FA Cup triumph against Leeds and their European goalkeeper during that last, albeit fairly short‑lived, adventure in the Cup Winners’ Cup 53 years ago.View image in fullscreenSunderland put on an impressive fireworks display before their European comeback.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersKick-off was prefaced by a spine-tingling, ear-splitting preamble featuring a giant tifo of a sailing ship floating above the message: “New shores to conquer”.Not that AZ were inclined to surrender lightly. Leeroy Echteld’s team had enjoyed an unbeaten start to the season, winning five and drawing one of their opening Eredivisie games.Indeed they would have taken an early lead had Robin Roefs not extended a boot and kept out the dangerous Ro-Zangelo Daal’s low shot after he had been played in by the talented visiting No 10 Kees Smit.The moment had arrived for Le Fée to start raising the home tone and his half-volley duly tested Jari De Busser. Though De Busser was swiftly forced to push Kevin Danso’s fine shot over the bar, Sunderland almost came undone on the counterattack and it took an excellent interception on Trai Hume’s part to halt Ayoub Oufkir.Quick GuideBenfica dispatch Amorim's MilanShowRuben Amorim’s Milan were beaten 2-0 by Marco Silva’s Benfica in the Europa League. Dodi Lukebakio put the Portuguese side ahead at San Siro in the 16th minute and Jakub Kaminski added a second early in the second half.Bayer Leverkusen, finalists in 2024, began their Europa League campaign with a 2-0 win against the Slovenian champions Celje while Lyon were 2-1 winners at Anderlecht.The Cypriot championsOmonia Nicosiastunned the La Liga sideCelta Vigo1-0 while Rangers’ conquerorsJagiellonia Bialystokwere denied a point at the Greek giantsOlympiacosby Roman Yaremchuk’s late winner.Sparta PraguethrashedArarat-Armenia4-1 whileSturm GrazagainstRennesandHapoel Be’er ShevaversusDinamo Zagrebboth ended goalless.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Smit and his teammates issued plenty of reminders that AZ are more than merely deft in possession, but Le Bris’s starting XI was hardly shabby either and, after Wilson Isidor conjured a glorious chance, Le Fée’s shot hit the post.It was not long before another shot, from Hume this time, whizzed just wide of an upright. When, back in January 2022, Hume joined Sunderland, they were still in League One.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBack in the present Le Bris’s team ended the first half thoroughly dominant yet frustrated. The manager later blamed “overthinking”. Oufkir, meanwhile, was arguably fortunate to collect only a yellow card after sliding in recklessly on Le Fée and was replaced by Weslley Patati at the interval.AZ re-emerged for the second half invigorated and, as Smit wrong‑footed Sunderland’s rearguard before curling a shot inches wide, it was easy to see why he has collected so many admirers across Europe.View image in fullscreenLe Fée fires home the decisive penalty.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersPerhaps anxious not to be upstaged, Le Fée swiftly regained the limelight courtesy of a stellar pass that Isidor could not quite polish off.When Hume subsequently missed another presentable chance it seemed that De Busser’s goal must be protected by some sort of magnetic forcefield.Then Patati felled Le Fée in the area as he shaped to shoot and a player being scrutinised by the France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, stepped up to the spot.Having seen a penalty against Arsenal saved expertly by David Raya last Saturday, Le Fée looked a little nervous but he sent De Busser the wrong way as he struck a textbook kick low into the bottom corner. “It was important to score,” Le Bris said. “But Enzo stepped up with bravery and courage. He’s resilient.”Although Nordi Mukiele and Brian Brobbey, on as a substitute, should really have doubled the lead before Patati’s volley almost provided a late equaliser for AZ, that penalty proved just enough to launch Sunderland’s galleon on European waters.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueSunderlandAZ AlkmaarEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Colin Kaepernick says NFL owners are colluding against Macklemore after Ed Sheeran tour ban | Colin Kaepernick | The Guardian
description: Colin Kaepernick has accused NFL owners of colluding against Macklemore after the rapper was removed from Ed Sheeran’s tour over comments on Palestine
Author: Tom Lutz
Headline: Colin Kaepernick has accused NFL owners of colluding against Macklemore after the rapper was removed from Ed Sheeran’s tour over comments on Palestine
Content: Colin Kaepernick has become a social activist since the end of his NFL career.Photograph: Kevin Wolf/APView image in fullscreenColin Kaepernick has become a social activist since the end of his NFL career.Photograph: Kevin Wolf/APColin KaepernickColin Kaepernick says NFL owners are colluding against Macklemore after Ed Sheeran tour banRapper dropped from tour after pro-Palestine remarksFormer NFL star settled case over collusion in 2019Tom LutzWed 16 Sep 2026 15.23 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 15.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleColin Kaepernick has accused NFL owners of colluding against Macklemore after the rapperwas removed from Ed Sheeran’s tourover comments he made onstage about Palestine.Kaepernick,whose NFL career was effectively endedin the wake of his protests against police violence, says he sees parallels between himself and Macklemore.Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard BryantRead more“The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what [New England Patriots owner] Robert Kraft and what they’re saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude,” Kaepernick said on theMeidasTouch podcast. “The [NFL owners] are openly colluding.”Macklemore had been a supporting act on Ed Sheeran’s tour. During an appearance at New Jersey’s MetLife stadium he told the crowd he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”. He also said “free Palestine”.Kraft, who is a longtime supporter of Israel, and several other owners of NFL stadiums the tour was due to visit said they would not let Macklemore play at their venues. This prompted Macklemore to be removed from the tour. All four supporting acts for upcoming dates of Sheeran’s tourhave since withdrawnin support of Macklemore.During the 2016 NFL season, Kaepernick began kneeling during the national anthem in protest at police brutality and social injustice. Despite being in his prime, Kaepernick was not signed by any NFL team after he left the San Francisco 49ers at the end of that season, and he has not played in the league since. He filed a grievance against the NFL in 2017, andthe case was settled in 2019with terms of the agreement undisclosed.Kaepernick told the MeidasTouch podcast that Kraft and other NFL owners had tried to hound outMacklemorein a similar way they did to him.“When we filed the grievance, it was like, well, the owners wouldn’t do that,” Kaepernick said. “Everybody just wants to win within theNFL. And the realization is, no. They want to protect their interests. They want to protect their power. They want to protect their money. And they also want people to know that if you take an action that they don’t agree with, they will come for you.”Kraft has said his decision to ban Macklemore from the Patriots’ stadium was due to his “recent actions” and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.Kaepernick said others may find themselves in a similar situation to Macklemore in the future.“It may not touch you today, at some point it’s going to come knocking on your doorstep or someone you love’s doorstep and that’s not the moment to be able to take action,” he said. “We should be taking action actively right now.”Elsewhere on Wednesday, NBA star Kyrie Irving said he would pay a $11,492 fine the NFL gave to Azeez Al-Shair after he displayed the name of a Palestinian girl killed byIsraelduring a game. Al-Shair did so using a face marking banned by the league.Explore more on these topicsColin KaepernickMacklemoreEd SheeranNFLIsraelPalestineUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Why can’t it be 100 times more popular?’: Ohanian aims high with women’s Athlos meeting | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Keely Hodgkinson and Gaby Thomas among the stars at London event whose promoter, Alexis Ohanian, has big plans and hopes for women’s sport
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Keely Hodgkinson and Gaby Thomas among the stars at London event whose promoter, Alexis Ohanian, has big plans and hopes for women’s sport
Content: Serena Williams with her eldest daughter, Olympia, and her husband, Alexis Ohanian, whose Athlos meeting comes to London on Friday.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenSerena Williams with her eldest daughter, Olympia, and her husband, Alexis Ohanian, whose Athlos meeting comes to London on Friday.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAthletics‘Why can’t it be 100 times more popular?’: Ohanian aims high with women’s Athlos meetingKeely Hodgkinson and Gaby Thomas among the stars at London event whose promoter, Alexis Ohanian, has big plans and hopes for women’s sportSean IngleWed 16 Sep 2026 16.45 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe timing could hardly be better. After a week when the discourse around women’s sport has been dominated by the actor Sydney Sweeney posing naked – and theintense backlash and counter-backlash– London will stage a major all-female track‑and‑field event on Friday.A sell-out crowd at the Athlos meeting at the StoneX Stadium in Hendon will feature Britain’s Keely Hodgkinson, along with the American stars Gabby Thomas and Tara Davis-Woodhall, competing for a prize fund of $1m (£750,000). There will be a red-carpet parade, celebrities galore and a celebration of the best of female sport.Hunt and Kerr have lit up summer, but will star athletes make Spoty shortlist?Read moreThe man behind it all, the US entrepreneur and investor Alexis Ohanian, believes this is just the start. Having made millions after cofounding the social media platform Reddit, and having set up the Angel City FC women’s football team, he is betting that track and field will thrive because of to the running boom and the Los Angeles Olympics.“You can’t go anywhere without seeing joggers, runners and run clubs,” he says. “London is a hotbed for it; the US, too. It is such an accessible sport. So why can’t it be a hundred times more popular? Or even a thousand times more popular?”We will talk more about that later, but Ohanian also has thoughts on Sweeney’s controversial advert for the US sports prediction company Novig, and the reaction from hundreds of female athletes from around the globe. He is also aware that Sweeney then retaliated by sharing covers of semi‑nude athletes from ESPN magazine’s Body Issue, including one of Ohanian’s wife, Serena Williams – a post that many took to be implying hypocrisy among her critics.“I’m not even mad,” Ohanian says. “If she wants to be naked for a commercial, that’s great, fine. It’s the false equivalence that I really support our athletes calling out about. The irony is my feed, at least, has been full of women athletes showing off, doing great women athlete stuff, which is awesome.”Ohanian also says that when an athlete poses for ESPN or Sports Illustrated it is very different. “You don’t have to look very hard to find reasons to celebrate actual women athletes. There’s a ton of them. They have massive followings. They have incredible stories. And, you know, them deciding to do an ESPN Body Issue is very obviously different from an actress just being naked for a commercial.“These are professional athletes who have devoted decades of their life towards a physical goal and their body is their résumé. So I have no problem understanding why it is totally OK for an athlete, man or woman, to pose naked tastefully. They are physically fit and showing it off because they grinded in the gym every morning to play football, ski, or whatever the hell they do.” ”View image in fullscreenKeely Hodgkinson is among the big names competing at the Athlos Meeting.Photograph: Dénes Erdős/APOhanian makes for engaging company. But he is never more passionate than when making the case that women’s sports will be far bigger in a decade. “Ten years from now, there will be multiple billion-dollar women’s teams in basketball and soccer, and they will be doing at least a hundred million in revenue easily,” he says. “And Chelsea will be the first in England.“The quality of play is also going to go up, because now there’s a business behind women’s sport,” he says, pointing to how a young girl will get far better coaching and support than 10 or 20 years ago, as money and standards rise. “Women’s tennis is an example of this because you can see the impact Serena and Venus made, where a decade later, the entire nature of women’s tennis looks very different. Consciousness is warped by, or moulded by, excellence.”Ohanian’s journey into investing in women’s sport began in March 2019 when he started tweeting about how women’s football must be hugely undervalued given the USA women’s soccer team was so successful and had millions of followers. “I laid this all out in a rant and I finished it by saying: ‘I’m going to either start a team, or buy one, and who can help?’”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe USA soccer star Alex Morgan replied. Soon afterwards Ohanian backed words with his wallet by launching Angel City FC. Having invested $7m, the club are now worth £$350m.“It was one of the first things I did after leaving Reddit. And I feel so blessed that it went on to be so successful so quickly, and had such a ripple effect of investment around women’s sports. For me, the lens after leaving Reddit is everything I build going forward is going to be something I’m really proud to tell my kids.”So why is he betting big on track and field? “When the Olympics were coming to LA, I said: ‘OK, what’s another sport where you have this massive popularity every four years and then it goes to zero?’ We have 300 million-plus people in America who love sport, who love cheering our athletes during the Olympics, but have no clue outside of that what’s going on. And that’s what I want to break.“I love the fact it’s the oldest sport. It’s immediately understandable – my eight‑year‑old can understand who wins. You can tell the entire story of an event in a short-form video. It’s perfect for the digital age. There’s a beauty to it. And it is high stakes. As soon as that gun goes off, you know you can’t blink.”Ohanian also promises that Athlos will end up a very different proposition to Grand Slam Track, the Michael Johnson-led venture thatfiled for bankruptcyafter three events last year. “We held our first race five months after our announcement in 2024 and 3.25 million people tuned in,” he says. “We had brands like Tiffany, who are not from this world, to be a part of this. And most importantly the athletes had a great time, got paid, and it was great.“But this is just the start. By 2036 I want us to have at least half a dozen races in the cities that are important stops in the calendar for these athletes.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing | England | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, but accepts he made them too early
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, but accepts he made them too early
Content: Thomas Tuchel said ‘the level of craziness Argentina put in’ influenced his decisions.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel said ‘the level of craziness Argentina put in’ influenced his decisions.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAEngland‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timingCoach says Argentina’s gung-ho approach forced hand‘No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more’Press AssociationWed 16 Sep 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cupsemi-final defeat against Argentinathis summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early.Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour. He said fatigue and the success of defending with a back five in knockout gamesagainst MexicoandNorwayalso influenced his decisions to sit on the lead.‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World CupRead moreThat approach proved catastrophic as goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez in the final stages of the game ended England’s dreams of making a first World Cup final since 1966.“You can try to kill me here. But it’s my scar, it’s not your scar,” Tuchel said in a documentary on the England app. “No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more. They can endlessly torture you and think: ‘If I had done different substitutions, then we would have won the match.’ You just don’t know it.“Of course you could [have made attacking changes]. No one knows what would have happened. We could have done it and maybe lost 2‑1 and could have gone: ‘Is he crazy? He finished the game against Norway with a back five, why didn’t he finish the game with five?’ I think from what I saw and the experience, the information and the level of crazinessArgentinaput in – change after change after change, it was just one offensive change after the other. That was my solution to the problem.“That’s what the intervention of a coach is. I try to help, you don’t implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.”View image in fullscreenJordan Pickford is beaten by Enzo Fernández’s shot for Argentina’s first goal.Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/ReutersEngland were on the back foot after scoring, with Djed Spence making a last-ditch tackle and Jordan Pickford making a big save immediately before the hydration break. It was then when Tuchel made his ill-fated decision to replace the goalscorer Gordon with the defender Ezri Konsa.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe German, who faced calls to be sacked in the aftermath of the semi-final defeat, insists the opposition’s gung-ho tactics forced his hand. “Argentina then play very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, [they played] fuck-it football: ‘We have nothing to lose. Let’s fuck it.’ A key moment if I look back at it and what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break. And I thought: ‘We will not survive. This is waiting for death. We don’t have ball possession, we’re not defending good, we’re not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.’“I changed to a 5-3-2, we changed the structure. Because I believe we can handle the width better and we still have three central defenders in the middle if crosses still fly in. We changed then to a 5-4-1. Even my mindset is maybe like: ‘Let’s just overcome it.’ And it’s too early. Too early for that mindset.”Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelArgentinaWorld Cup 2026newsShareReuse this content

title: Tammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at Coventry | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: The forward scored his first goals of the season in Aston Villa’s 3-1 win at Coventry, who levelled through Victor Torp, in the Carabao Cup third round
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: The forward scored his first goals of the season in Aston Villa’s 3-1 win at Coventry, who levelled through Victor Torp, in the Carabao Cup third round
Content: Tammy Abraham shows his delight after scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAView image in fullscreenTammy Abraham shows his delight after scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PACarabao CupTammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at CoventryBen Fisherat the Coventry Building Society ArenaWed 16 Sep 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleForAston Villa, an overdue drama-free outing as Unai Emery’s side cruised into the Carabao Cup fourth round courtesy of a Tammy Abraham double and a Ross Barkley header.The satisfaction was detectable in Emery’s voice as he reflected on a night of positives: Abraham’s first goals of the season, Ibrahim Mbaye’s encouraging full debut and another half-hour for the £52m club-record signing, Johan Manzambi. Are things clicking into gear after a summer of changes?De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comebackRead moreUnfortunately for Coventry, it was a sorry case of more of the same. Frank Lampard’s side have lost five of their six matches in all competitions, across which they have leaked 15 goals. It was hard to know whether Abraham’s tap-in or Barkley’s free header, both from corners, was worse from a Coventry perspective. The sight of Lampard hunched in the dugout, hands clasped, has become a familiar sight. “If you give two set pieces away as simply as we did, it’s quite hard to win against Premier League opposition,” the Coventry head coach said.Lampard’s side, who have lost their opening league four matches by an aggregate of 10-0 and on Saturday visit Nottingham Forest hoping for lift-off, are yet to score outside this competition. Victor Torp’s sweet free-kick from the edge of Villa’s 18-yard box, to cancel out Abraham’s opener, represented Coventry’s first goal since Torpcapped the scoring at Plymouthin the previous round. This victory earned Villa a fourth-round trip to Bournemouth at the end of October.This was the first competitive meeting between these sides since 5 May 2001, when Coventry’s initial 34-year stay in the top flight came to an end with a 3-2 defeat at Villa Park. When Aurèle Amenda limped off with a calf injury after 10 minutes, Bobby Thomas, wearing the captain’s armband, was the only player left of the starting lineup from Sunday’s5-0 home defeat against Brighton.Emery made seven changes himself and George Hemmings, one of those to keep their place, was the architect for Villa’s opener. Matteo Ruggeri fed Hemmings down the left and the 19-year-old sent a sumptuous pass into Abraham with the outside of his right boot.View image in fullscreenFrank Lampard shows his disappointment as Coventry suffer another defeat.Photograph: Getty Images/Sportsphoto/AllstarCoventry struggled to retain possession and Villa were enjoying themselves, exchanging crisp, clean passes. But then Barkley was penalised for fouling Caleb Yirenkyi on the edge of the Villa box and Torp stepped up to lift the subsequent free-kick over the Villa wall. John McGinn, the Villa captain reduced to the role of draught excluder, picked himself up from the turf.Quick GuideCarabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over BladesShowA 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sentFleetwoodinto the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents,Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw.Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory.Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net.United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide.Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean.Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal.United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked.Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win overWolvesthree minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute.It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Suddenly Coventry were full of confidence, a little giddy. Thomas moonlighted as a striker, forcing an error from Tyrone Mings, but then declined a golden opportunity to shoot at goal and the chance fizzled out. Gustavo Hamer then whistled a left-foot shot just past a Villa upright.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCoventry sprung to life but Villa responded. McGinn smacked his hands together after spurning a decent chance and a few minutes later Barkley sent a low drive at goal that Dan Bentley did well to push wide for a corner, from which Villa prospered. Mbaye’s inswinging delivery was on the money and Barkley, totally unmarked in the six-yard box, headed in at the front post.Coventry had the meanest defence in the Championship last season but have been porous since promotion. More slack marking enabled Villa to extend their lead. McGinn whipped a corner into the six-yard box and Abraham prodded in after walking off his marker, the 18-year-old Coventry debutant Stephen Mfuni, who this month joined on loan from Manchester City.Abraham’s second gave Villa breathing space. Emery, whose side visit Tottenham on Saturday, felt comfortable enough to withdraw McGinn and Mbaye just after the hour. Zion Suzuki replaced the injured Marco Bizot at half-time, the goalkeeper reporting a back problem. Nicolas Jackson later came on in place of Abraham. Emery cycled through the changes but Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since signing, remained on the bench.“He is progressing but we have players in front of him now,” Emery said. “George is playing fantastic, Alysson is understanding a lot of things very good; he needs time but he is giving us things I want. Mbaye responded well. We want a competitive team and the players ready to compete on the standard we have. Of course, he [Garnacho] is a little bit behind because of some circumstances he had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupCoventry CityAston Villamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Sky closes in on broadcast rights for first women’s British & Irish Lions tour | Women's rugby union | The Guardian
description: The inaugural British & Irish Lions tour of New Zealand in 2027 is expected to be broadcast live on Sky Sports
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The inaugural British & Irish Lions tour of New Zealand in 2027 is expected to be broadcast live on Sky Sports
Content: Jo Yapp is the women’s British & Irish Lions head coach and they will tour New Zealand in September 2027.Photograph: Dan Sheridan/Inpho/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJo Yapp is the women’s British & Irish Lions head coach and they will tour New Zealand in September 2027.Photograph: Dan Sheridan/Inpho/ShutterstockWomen's rugby unionSky closes in on broadcast rights for first women’s British & Irish Lions tourLions to play five fixtures in New Zealand in 2027Sky has held live rights for men’s Lions since 1997Exclusive byMatt HughesWed 16 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 03.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe inaugural women’s British & Irish Lions tour of New Zealand next year is expected to be broadcast live onSky Sportsin a significant boost for the women’s game. Sky has held live rights for men’s Lions fixtures since the 1997 tour of South Africa, and the broadcaster is understood to be in advanced discussions about adding the women’s series to its portfolio.England survive sluggish start to overwhelm Australia in second halfRead moreThe first women’s Lions will play three Tests against the Black Ferns and two tour matches next September, with Sky expected to broadcast all five fixtures.Sky’s willingness to bid for the rights is a timely fillip for the sport given the disappointment expressed by Rugby Football Union officials at the BBC’s decision to limit its coverage of the Red Roses’ three home Tests this month to its red button and online channels.The Red Roses have been regulars on BBC Two in recent years, but the main channel was showing the 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia last Saturday afternoon while the world champions were beating Australia 48-15 at Sale Sharks’ CorpAcq Stadium.Sky’s investment in rugby union has dipped in recent years and it no longer broadcasts regular internationals or club matches, but it remains committed to its longstanding association with the Lions.Talks are also taking place about extending the contract with the men’s Lions to cover the 2029 series, which will also take place in New Zealand.The women’s Lions were launched in 2024 after a three-year feasibility study and, while France was also considered, New Zealand was confirmed that year as the destination for their first tour.The Lions sprang a surprise this year by appointing the former England captain Jo Yapp as their first women’s head coach in preference to the Red Roses’ coach, John Mitchell. Yapp has started working for the Lions in a part-time capacity in conjunction with her existing role as head of the Rugby Football Union’s women’s pathway, but she will go full-time for the tourists at the start of next year.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSky was contacted for comment.Explore more on these topicsWomen's rugby unionBritish & Irish LionsSky SportsRugby unionSports rightsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Matt Fitzpatrick casts doubt on Dubai title defence over fears about conflict | European Tour | The Guardian
description: The world No 4 said he was ‘not comfortable’ appearing at the DP World Tour’s season-closing events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai amid the Middle East conflict
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: The world No 4 said he was ‘not comfortable’ appearing at the DP World Tour’s season-closing events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai amid the Middle East conflict
Content: Matt Fitzpatrick says he would be wary of travelling to the Middle East after having a child in August.Photograph: Colin Hubbard/APView image in fullscreenMatt Fitzpatrick says he would be wary of travelling to the Middle East after having a child in August.Photograph: Colin Hubbard/APEuropean TourMatt Fitzpatrick casts doubt on Dubai title defence over fears about conflictWorld No 4 may snub World Tour Championship‘I’m not comfortable playing in the Middle East’Ewan Murrayat WentworthWed 16 Sep 2026 11.01 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMatt Fitzpatrick, the world No 4, has admitted to reservations over appearing at the DP World Tour’s end‑of‑season events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai because of the conflict in the Middle East.The Englishman, who is due to defend the DP World Tour Championship title in Dubai, has accused the tour of being “very vague” over plans to retain or move the tournaments. In Fitzpatrick’s mind, it is a “no-brainer” to play elsewhere, but he believes his sentiment will not feature strongly in the thoughts of the tour’s hierarchy.Fitzpatrick even suggested that Formula One is reconsidering staging the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in December after races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were called off this year because of the Iran war, though itremains on the calendar.Top golfers to get no favours for PGA Tour return after LIV bankruptcyRead moreThe Abu Dhabi Championship is due to take place from 5 November, with the DP World Tour Championship slated for the following week. Every indication is that those competitions will happen in the United Arab Emirates, despite contingencies involving Turkey, Spain and Portugal known to have been considered.“As things stand right now, I would say I’m not that comfortable,” Fitzpatrick said about playing in the Middle East. “A few things have changed for me. I had a child in August and that changes things a bit more.“It would feel a little bit weird, given what I’m reading elsewhere. Things can change overnight, I’m sure. I think it seems to be going down that path of things are getting better. I’ve looked on the UK [government] website, I know they changed it from essential travel only to one step better than that.“I know the tour has been on this for a long time. It’s frustrating the decision hasn’t been made so you can plan. But I understand there’s a lot of moving parts to that and it’s difficult to make these decisions.“If the tour do go, I’m sure they have had the best advice possible on what that looks like. As things stand, I wouldn’t necessarily be too keen on going. I know there’s been discussions on what Formula One is doing. I’ve heard they might not be going there, so it begs the question, would we, I guess.”Fitzpatrick later made reference to missile strike damage to a hotel in Dubai where he had dinner in the week of his 2025 win at JumeirahGolfEstates. “That’s very scary,” he said.” Pressed on whether he felt his viewpoint would be heeded, Fitzpatrick said: “I don’t think so.”Fitzpatrick said his management was informed in April that the tour would make a decision by June. “I’m sure the Middle East want the DP World Tour to go there badly because it’s a great event for two weeks. It’s great for tourism and all that sort of stuff with it, but I wouldn’t say that I have had regular contact.“It’s been very vague the whole time and they have not necessarily kind of had open communication.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMatt Fitzpatrick is due to defend the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty ImagesThe topic is a rising one for discussion this week at the PGA Championship, the DP World Tour’s flagship competition, at Wentworth. A spokesperson for the DP World Tour said: “We are in constant dialogue with our members and their management teams about the tournaments they play in but ultimately players’ individual schedule choices are a matter for them to decide.“As far as our playoffs are concerned, it remains our intention to play as scheduled in the UAE, but we continue to monitor the situation and take advice from our international travel advisers.”Should Fitzpatrick and others opt to skip UAE-based tournaments, it would clearly undermine their status. Rory McIlroy is seeking to win a record-equalling eighth European order of merit – now the Race to Dubai – title.The Open champion, Ryan Fox, is content to be guided by the tour. “There are some concerns,” the New Zealander said. “I’m of the opinion that the tour is doing their due diligence. If they feel like it’s safe for us to go, I’m willing to support that.“But I can understand, also, why guys have some reservations. I’ll keep monitoring it. If I feel like it’s not the right decision, I might not go, but at this point I trust the tour’s decision in that regard.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean TourGolfnewsShareReuse this content

title: Greens just four points behind Labour in urban areas, poll reveals | Green party | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: UK’s Green parties could take 40 seats if result replicated at next election, according to Labour-linked thinktank
Author: Kiran Stacey
Headline: Exclusive: UK’s Green parties could take 40 seats if result replicated at next election, according to Labour-linked thinktank
Content: Zack Polanski, leader of the Green party of England and Wales, is standing for parliament in Keir Starmer’s former constituency.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAView image in fullscreenZack Polanski, leader of the Green party of England and Wales, is standing for parliament in Keir Starmer’s former constituency.Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPAGreen partyGreens just four points behind Labour in urban areas, poll revealsExclusive: UK’s Green parties could take 40 seats if result replicated at next election, according to Labour-linked thinktankKiran StaceyPolicy editorWed 16 Sep 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Greens are just four points behindLabourin urban constituencies across the UK, putting them within touching distance of taking as many as 40 seats if the result was replicated at the next election, according to new polling by a Labour-linked thinktank.The survey by ThinkLabour, which has extensive links to Andy Burnham’s government, finds that urban voters have moved in large numbers towards the UK’s Green parties since the 2024 general election. The research highlights the challenge Labour faces inholding on to the Holborn and St Pancras seatin the face of a challenge from Zack Polanski, the party leader in England and Wales, at next month’s byelection.The study’s authors warn that evidence from previous electoral battles between the two parties suggests Labour politicians should dial down direct attacks on the Greens for fear of looking as if they are “kicking a puppy”.Christabel Cooper, one of the report’s authors, said: “The previous administration [under Keir Starmer] had always banked on the fact that Labour would be able to say to people who vote Green that they would get Nigel Farage as prime minister.“But in the 40 seats that we have identified, that is no longer the case – the Greens can claim to be the progressives’ party of choice.”She added that evidence from other elections where the party has gone head to head with Labour suggests that progressives dislike aggressive attacks on the Greens.“The sorts of people who would consider voting Labour consider attacking the Greens like kicking a puppy. They think, we are all supposed to be nice and liberal, why are we having a go at the Greens?”The findings, which have been discussed with strategists in No 10 as they look to solidify separate polling gains made in Burnham’s early weeks as prime minister, show Labour faces a difficult task winning back urban progressives who helped the party win the last election.ThinkLabour’s former chief executive Alison Phillips is now Burnham’s chief of staff, while other alumni of the organisation have senior roles across government.The research was carried out as Burnham was about to take office in Downing Street, meaning it will not have captured the full effect of the “Burnham bounce”, which has seen Labour gain ground with progressive voters and pull level with Reform UK.The poll shows that support for the Greens has increased by 12 points in major cities since the general election, while Labour’s vote share has fallen by 20 points, leaving Labour only 4 points ahead in some of its most reliable strongholds.It found that the move from Labour to the Greens has been more pronounced among voters who are financially struggling, undermining the stereotype of Green voters as affluent liberals.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion‘We can win here’: Zack Polanski presses the flesh in Holborn and St PancrasRead moreThe report warned that urban voters felt they did not know what Labour’s values were, in part because of some of the counterintuitive measures taken by Starmer in his early days as prime minister, such as cutting winter fuel payments.It also warns that winning these voters back will mean focusing immigration reforms on tackling small boat crossings rather than wider measures to tackle legal migration.Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, is bringing in measures to make it harder for legal migrants to achieve settled status, which haveproved controversialwith Labour MPs and activists.The report said: “On divisive areas such as immigration, where liberals and social conservatives can agree on some outcomes – reducing small boat crossings, for example – it should primarily focus on these.“Where its policies appear tough or restrictive, Labour must be able to make a convincing progressive case for them, showing how they solve practical problems rather than simply signalling to the right.”The researchers also found that attacks on the Greens over foreign policy had the most effect with the voters Labour is trying to win back, in part because they found these more credible than other criticisms.While urban voters did not like Green policies on legalising drugs – which Labour focused on during the failed campaign to win the Gorton and Denton byelection – they did not view them as a particularly credible threat.Personal attacks on Polanski, meanwhile, went down badly among those considering voting Green, who viewed criticisms of his CV and his past as a hypnotherapist as especially non-credible.The Green leader has previously come under fire fortelling a journalistin 2013 he could enlarge women’s breasts with hypnotherapy – comments he has since said he regrets.Explore more on these topicsGreen partyLabourZack PolanskiHolborn and St Pancras byelectionImmigration and asylumnewsShareReuse this content

title: US lawmakers pass bill giving Trump more power to sanction Russia and its enablers | Trump tariffs | The Guardian
description: Act divides Democrats and Republicans, with some saying it gives president power that could be turned against US allies
Author: Andrew Roth
Headline: Act divides Democrats and Republicans, with some saying it gives president power that could be turned against US allies
Content: Buildings heavily damaged following a Russian missile attack in Sloviansk, Donetsk region, UkrainePhotograph: Cameron Jones-Manley/Zuma Press/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBuildings heavily damaged following a Russian missile attack in Sloviansk, Donetsk region, UkrainePhotograph: Cameron Jones-Manley/Zuma Press/ShutterstockTrump tariffsUS lawmakers pass bill giving Trump more power to sanction Russia and its enablersAct divides Democrats and Republicans, with some saying it gives president power that could be turned against US alliesAndrew RothWed 16 Sep 2026 18.41 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 19.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe US Congress has passed a sweeping bill allowingDonald Trumpto raise tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy and issue other punishing sanctions against the Kremlin following a pitched battle between lawmakers backing Ukraine and sceptics worried the bill gives the president too much power.The Lindsey O Graham SanctioningRussiaand Iran Act of 2026 passed in a 262-159 vote on the last day before Congress goes on recess ahead of the midterm elections. Graham, who died earlier this year, co-authored and submitted the bill more than a year and a half ago.The long delay in the vote was widely considered to be scepticism from theTrump administration, which had opposed additional sanctions and then recently changed its stance to support tabling the bill as efforts to negotiate with the Kremlin to end the war have yielded few results.However the bill faced last-minute hurdles in Congress as members of the Republican party’s isolationist wing were joined by Democrats who warned that Trump could use the bill’s new tariffs authority against allies instead.The bill would mandate new sanctions on Russian political and military officials, and foreign networks helping to supply Russia’s war machine and evade existing sanctions. It would also target Russia’s so-called fleet of “shadow tankers”, which have allowed the country to continue to ship crude around the world despite sanctions on its energy exports.It would also allow Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top purchasers of Russian energy, including China, as well as other countries helping the Kremlin evade sanctions.Senior Democrats voiced opposition to the bill during a heated floor debate. “Why in the world would this Congress give this president additional authority to visit that kind of economic harm on the American people?” said Hakeem Jeffries, the leading Democrat in the House, during a speech on Wednesday, adding he would vote against the bill.Democratic staffers supporting the bill said that it offered a “last chance” to increase sanctions on Russia before Ukraine entered a “long winter”. Russia has improved the drone technology it has used to strike Ukrainian infrastructure as Kyiv has suffered a shortage of anti-air missiles, leaving the country in a dire position.Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican supporting the bill, called it the US Congress’ “Churchill vs Chamberlain Moment on Russia”.“Choking off the money funding a war of conquest in Europe is exactly what that authority should be used for, and Congress deciding to do that is Congress doing its constitutional job,” he said, rejecting arguments by Democrats that the bill gave Trump too much authority to slap tariffs on foreign countries.The bill passed the Senate last month in a landslide 86-11 vote. However it faced more pushback in the House of Representatives. A Tuesday rule vote allowing consideration of Senate amendments to the bill passed by just 214-211, with two renegade Democrats joining Republicans to vote in favour of what they said was an act of support for Ukraine. That vote led to senior Democrats holding terse talks with their fellow party members.“I’m proud to represent one of the largest Ukrainian communities in America – people who have lost fathers, mothers, sons and daughters in the fight to defeat fascism,” wrote Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, one of the two Democrat representatives, in a statement on Tuesday.“I’ll always stand with my community’s values, and am grateful for the 86 senators who voted to send this bill to the House. My vote today gets us one step closer to enacting these sanctions into law and I look forward to voting tomorrow to cut off the flow of Russian oil money fuelling this war.”The Ukrainian government has said it supported the bill, and hundreds of pro-Ukrainian activists calling for tougher sanctions on Russia held advocacy talks in Washington DC in the days leading up to the vote.“We support any initiative that is in the interest of Ukraine and Ukrainians,” said Denys Sienik, the Chargé d’Affaires at the Ukrainian embassy in Washington DC. “So if we are talking about the possibility of putting more pressure on Russia so that it holds the Russian war machine, of course, we are there, and we are grateful to every senator, to every congressman and congresswoman for their voice and, and for their support.”Explore more on these topicsTrump tariffsDonald TrumpTrump administrationUS CongressUS politicsTariffsRussianewsShareReuse this content

title: Nato leader warns of ‘most dangerous and complex security environment in a generation’ | World news | The Guardian
description: Mark Rutte asks UK and Europe to ‘provide hard power Nato needs’ in face of geopolitical uncertainty
Author: Dan Sabbagh
Headline: Mark Rutte asks UK and Europe to ‘provide hard power Nato needs’ in face of geopolitical uncertainty
Content: NATO secretary general Mark Rutte discussed Britain’s Nato commitments with Andy Burnham during their first one-on-one meeting.Photograph: Neil Hall/EPAView image in fullscreenNATO secretary general Mark Rutte discussed Britain’s Nato commitments with Andy Burnham during their first one-on-one meeting.Photograph: Neil Hall/EPAWorld newsNato leader warns of ‘most dangerous and complex security environment in a generation’Mark Rutte asks UK and Europe to ‘provide hard power Nato needs’ in face of geopolitical uncertaintyDan SabbaghDefence and security editorWed 16 Sep 2026 14.46 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNato needs “more UK and more Europe” to deal with the most dangerous security environment faced by the west in a generation, the secretary general of the 32-country military alliance said this afternoon on a visit to the UK.Mark Rutte praised Britain for promising to increase defence spending in line with US demands after a meeting prime ministerAndy Burnham– but argued that the military and financial effort must continue into the future.“It is essential that your armed forces continue to provide the hard power Nato needs,” Rutte said in a speech to a specialist audience at Ditchley Park, a wartime retreat used by Winston Churchill in Oxfordshire.It was a plea for the UK to make progress towards an alliance-wide target demanded by Donald Trump of spending 3.5% of GDP by 2035, about £30bn in real terms, money that has to be found from extra taxation, borrowing or reducing other spending.Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter as Nato jets shoot down drone over LithuaniaRead moreBritain has so far only budgeted to increase defence spending to 2.7% of GDP by the end of the next decade.
