Having a successful college football team is a way of attracting students. “There’s real rationale behind it,” says Yormark. “About 14% of our student athletes are international, so how do you drive enrollment? How do you drive global appeal and fan engagement? All of that helps you to rationalise that going global does matter.”View image in fullscreenKansas are taking on Arizona in the match.Photograph: Hanover commsIs this the start of something bigger?“Our goal isn’t just to play here once,” says Yormark. “In sports, you’ve got to have continuity, you gotta build something. If there’s two Big 12 teams playing every year, British fans start gravitating to the Big 12 conference. They get to know our schools, our athletes, our coaches. Our ambition is to take many of our sports globally and take the conference global.”What sort of crowd do they expect?Young and loud. With ticket prices half what NFL International Games cost, the organisers are hoping for a crowd of 60,000. “That would be a tremendous number for us,” says Yormark. “We can build on it”. With family offers and cheap tickets for NHS and education workers, the event should beat the Big 12’s average attendance last year of 50,000.Wembley is attractive to promoters as they can still make a handsome profit even if only two-thirds of the seats are filled. It’s why the RFL have kept the Challenge Cup final at the stadium despite not selling it out. Several thousand fans from Arizona and Kansas are travelling over for the away game of a lifetime. The match should feel different to the NFL, too, with both teams flying over their huge marching bands and half a dozen performers booked in for the pre-match and half-time shows.“This isn’t just a game,” say the organisers. “It’s a full-scale celebration of sport, energy and culture: from pre-game tailgate parties and marching band pep rallies, to a half-time show that lights up the stadium.”View image in fullscreenKansas players celebrate during their match against Missouri earlier this month.Photograph: Jay Biggerstaff/Getty ImagesWhy are Arizona and Kansas playing?They volunteered. “Our schools were very excited about it, specifically Kansas, who said they wanted to move a home game to London. They were playing Arizona at home and Arizona were more than happy to come here,” says Yormark. The timing is perfect for Arizona,who have just opened a London branch, running a dozen or so degrees out of a University of London building in Clerkenwell.As for the players, they are very excited. “About 90% of the student athletes coming over didn’t have a passport,” says Yormark. “For them to enjoy a wonderful international experience, while playing the game they love, doesn’t get much better. The students’ experiences are the most important thing to us.”Follow No Helmets Required onFacebookExplore more on these topicsCollege sportsNo Helmets RequiredNFLUS sportsNCAAfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of club | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The club’s American chair left the club after the deal was secured and said: ‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The club’s American chair left the club after the deal was secured and said: ‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’
Content: ‘It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club,’ said Todd Boehly.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersView image in fullscreen‘It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club,’ said Todd Boehly.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersChelseaBoehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of clubAmerican chair Boehly leaves role after deal is secured‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’Press AssociationWed 16 Sep 2026 19.28 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 19.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTodd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes inChelseain a deal under which Clearlake Capital takes full control of the Premier League club.The American billionaire businessmen Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in a sale mandated by the UK government in May 2022. The private equity company Clearlake had previously owned 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjörg Wyss.Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark WalterRead moreA statement issued late on Wednesday night read: “Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, LP will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.“As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club.”Chelsea said Boehly, the chair, had shown “unwavering commitment” to the ownership group’s belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club. “The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success,” the statement added.“Under their joint ownership, substantial investment has been made across the men’s and women’s senior and youth squads, Chelsea’s training facilities at Cobham, medical and player-support resources, academy development and pathways, and the sporting and business leadership of the club.“Todd Boehly now leaves his role as chairman with Chelsea well positioned for the next phase of development. Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together.”View image in fullscreenXabi Alonso has been tasked with reviving Chelsea’s fortunes.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APBoehly said: “It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”Behdad Eghbali and José Feliciano, cofounders of Clearlake Capital, said: “Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.“Clearlake has served as Chelsea’s majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club’s infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club’s supporters.”Chelsea, who appointed Xabi Alonso as manager in the summer and are sixth in the Premier League, say there will be no changes to day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club.Explore more on these topicsChelseanewsShareReuse this content

title: Tammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at Coventry | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: The forward scored his first goals of the season in Aston Villa’s 3-1 win at Coventry, who levelled through Victor Torp, in the Carabao Cup third round
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: The forward scored his first goals of the season in Aston Villa’s 3-1 win at Coventry, who levelled through Victor Torp, in the Carabao Cup third round
Content: Tammy Abraham shows his delight after scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAView image in fullscreenTammy Abraham shows his delight after scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Nick Potts/PACarabao CupTammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at CoventryBen Fisherat the Coventry Building Society ArenaWed 16 Sep 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleForAston Villa, an overdue drama-free outing as Unai Emery’s side cruised into the Carabao Cup fourth round courtesy of a Tammy Abraham double and a Ross Barkley header.The satisfaction was detectable in Emery’s voice as he reflected on a night of positives: Abraham’s first goals of the season, Ibrahim Mbaye’s encouraging full debut and another half-hour for the £52m club-record signing, Johan Manzambi. Are things clicking into gear after a summer of changes?De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comebackRead moreUnfortunately for Coventry, it was a sorry case of more of the same. Frank Lampard’s side have lost five of their six matches in all competitions, across which they have leaked 15 goals. It was hard to know whether Abraham’s tap-in or Barkley’s free header, both from corners, was worse from a Coventry perspective. The sight of Lampard hunched in the dugout, hands clasped, has become a familiar sight. “If you give two set pieces away as simply as we did, it’s quite hard to win against Premier League opposition,” the Coventry head coach said.Lampard’s side, who have lost their opening league four matches by an aggregate of 10-0 and on Saturday visit Nottingham Forest hoping for lift-off, are yet to score outside this competition. Victor Torp’s sweet free-kick from the edge of Villa’s 18-yard box, to cancel out Abraham’s opener, represented Coventry’s first goal since Torpcapped the scoring at Plymouthin the previous round. This victory earned Villa a fourth-round trip to Bournemouth at the end of October.This was the first competitive meeting between these sides since 5 May 2001, when Coventry’s initial 34-year stay in the top flight came to an end with a 3-2 defeat at Villa Park. When Aurèle Amenda limped off with a calf injury after 10 minutes, Bobby Thomas, wearing the captain’s armband, was the only player left of the starting lineup from Sunday’s5-0 home defeat against Brighton.Emery made seven changes himself and George Hemmings, one of those to keep their place, was the architect for Villa’s opener. Matteo Ruggeri fed Hemmings down the left and the 19-year-old sent a sumptuous pass into Abraham with the outside of his right boot.View image in fullscreenFrank Lampard shows his disappointment as Coventry suffer another defeat.Photograph: Getty Images/Sportsphoto/AllstarCoventry struggled to retain possession and Villa were enjoying themselves, exchanging crisp, clean passes. But then Barkley was penalised for fouling Caleb Yirenkyi on the edge of the Villa box and Torp stepped up to lift the subsequent free-kick over the Villa wall. John McGinn, the Villa captain reduced to the role of draught excluder, picked himself up from the turf.Quick GuideCarabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over BladesShowA 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sentFleetwoodinto the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents,Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw.Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory.Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net.United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide.Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean.Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal.United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked.Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win overWolvesthree minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute.It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Suddenly Coventry were full of confidence, a little giddy. Thomas moonlighted as a striker, forcing an error from Tyrone Mings, but then declined a golden opportunity to shoot at goal and the chance fizzled out. Gustavo Hamer then whistled a left-foot shot just past a Villa upright.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCoventry sprung to life but Villa responded. McGinn smacked his hands together after spurning a decent chance and a few minutes later Barkley sent a low drive at goal that Dan Bentley did well to push wide for a corner, from which Villa prospered. Mbaye’s inswinging delivery was on the money and Barkley, totally unmarked in the six-yard box, headed in at the front post.Coventry had the meanest defence in the Championship last season but have been porous since promotion. More slack marking enabled Villa to extend their lead. McGinn whipped a corner into the six-yard box and Abraham prodded in after walking off his marker, the 18-year-old Coventry debutant Stephen Mfuni, who this month joined on loan from Manchester City.Abraham’s second gave Villa breathing space. Emery, whose side visit Tottenham on Saturday, felt comfortable enough to withdraw McGinn and Mbaye just after the hour. Zion Suzuki replaced the injured Marco Bizot at half-time, the goalkeeper reporting a back problem. Nicolas Jackson later came on in place of Abraham. Emery cycled through the changes but Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since signing, remained on the bench.“He is progressing but we have players in front of him now,” Emery said. “George is playing fantastic, Alysson is understanding a lot of things very good; he needs time but he is giving us things I want. Mbaye responded well. We want a competitive team and the players ready to compete on the standard we have. Of course, he [Garnacho] is a little bit behind because of some circumstances he had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupCoventry CityAston Villamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing | England | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, but accepts he made them too early
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, but accepts he made them too early
Content: Thomas Tuchel said ‘the level of craziness Argentina put in’ influenced his decisions.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel said ‘the level of craziness Argentina put in’ influenced his decisions.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAEngland‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timingCoach says Argentina’s gung-ho approach forced hand‘No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more’Press AssociationWed 16 Sep 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cupsemi-final defeat against Argentinathis summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early.Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour. He said fatigue and the success of defending with a back five in knockout gamesagainst MexicoandNorwayalso influenced his decisions to sit on the lead.‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World CupRead moreThat approach proved catastrophic as goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez in the final stages of the game ended England’s dreams of making a first World Cup final since 1966.“You can try to kill me here. But it’s my scar, it’s not your scar,” Tuchel said in a documentary on the England app. “No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more. They can endlessly torture you and think: ‘If I had done different substitutions, then we would have won the match.’ You just don’t know it.“Of course you could [have made attacking changes]. No one knows what would have happened. We could have done it and maybe lost 2‑1 and could have gone: ‘Is he crazy? He finished the game against Norway with a back five, why didn’t he finish the game with five?’ I think from what I saw and the experience, the information and the level of crazinessArgentinaput in – change after change after change, it was just one offensive change after the other. That was my solution to the problem.“That’s what the intervention of a coach is. I try to help, you don’t implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.”View image in fullscreenJordan Pickford is beaten by Enzo Fernández’s shot for Argentina’s first goal.Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/ReutersEngland were on the back foot after scoring, with Djed Spence making a last-ditch tackle and Jordan Pickford making a big save immediately before the hydration break. It was then when Tuchel made his ill-fated decision to replace the goalscorer Gordon with the defender Ezri Konsa.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe German, who faced calls to be sacked in the aftermath of the semi-final defeat, insists the opposition’s gung-ho tactics forced his hand. “Argentina then play very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, [they played] fuck-it football: ‘We have nothing to lose. Let’s fuck it.’ A key moment if I look back at it and what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break. And I thought: ‘We will not survive. This is waiting for death. We don’t have ball possession, we’re not defending good, we’re not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.’“I changed to a 5-3-2, we changed the structure. Because I believe we can handle the width better and we still have three central defenders in the middle if crosses still fly in. We changed then to a 5-4-1. Even my mindset is maybe like: ‘Let’s just overcome it.’ And it’s too early. Too early for that mindset.”Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelArgentinaWorld Cup 2026newsShareReuse this content

title: Enzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZ | Europa League | The Guardian
description: Four days after having a penalty saved against Arsenal, Enzo Le Fée scored from 12 yards as Sunderland won 1-0 against AZ in their Europa League opener
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Four days after having a penalty saved against Arsenal, Enzo Le Fée scored from 12 yards as Sunderland won 1-0 against AZ in their Europa League opener
Content: Enzo Le Fée punches the air after scoring the only goal of the game from 12 yards.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenEnzo Le Fée punches the air after scoring the only goal of the game from 12 yards.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersEuropa LeagueEnzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZLouise Taylorat the Stadium of LightWed 16 Sep 2026 17.06 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGranit Xhaka, Sunderland’s captain, believes it is not unrealistic to dream about Régis Le Bris’s side travelling all the way to theEuropa Leaguefinal next spring.It is rarely a good idea to dismiss Xhaka but reaching that showpiece in Frankfurt will necessitate considerably more efficient finishing on his team’s part than proved evident on a highly evocative night on Wearside.Sunderland 1-0 AZ, Milan 0-2 Benfica and more: Europa League clockwatch – liveRead moreThanks to a second-half penalty from the indefatigable Enzo Le Fée – appropriately the game’s outstanding player – the game ended happily forSunderlandas the home side launched their big return to Europe with a morale-boosting win.Along the way they missed a litany of chances but, in Le Fée, possessed both a high-calibre attacking playmaker and a tireless off‑the‑ball warrior who, time after time, regained possession for his team.When Le Bris was invited later to agree that a player he first coached as a 12-year-old in Lorient’s academy was Champions League class, the Sunderland manager’s smile lit up the room. “Enzo’s a great player,” he said. “I trust him and his quality. I’m proud and pleased for the players and the fans, AZ are a really good side but we played with heart and togetherness.”Occupants of the VIP seats included Jimmy Montgomery, the now 82-year-old hero of Sunderland’s 1973 FA Cup triumph against Leeds and their European goalkeeper during that last, albeit fairly short‑lived, adventure in the Cup Winners’ Cup 53 years ago.View image in fullscreenSunderland put on an impressive fireworks display before their European comeback.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersKick-off was prefaced by a spine-tingling, ear-splitting preamble featuring a giant tifo of a sailing ship floating above the message: “New shores to conquer”.Not that AZ were inclined to surrender lightly. Leeroy Echteld’s team had enjoyed an unbeaten start to the season, winning five and drawing one of their opening Eredivisie games.Indeed they would have taken an early lead had Robin Roefs not extended a boot and kept out the dangerous Ro-Zangelo Daal’s low shot after he had been played in by the talented visiting No 10 Kees Smit.The moment had arrived for Le Fée to start raising the home tone and his half-volley duly tested Jari De Busser. Though De Busser was swiftly forced to push Kevin Danso’s fine shot over the bar, Sunderland almost came undone on the counterattack and it took an excellent interception on Trai Hume’s part to halt Ayoub Oufkir.Quick GuideBenfica dispatch Amorim's MilanShowRuben Amorim’s Milan were beaten 2-0 by Marco Silva’s Benfica in the Europa League. Dodi Lukebakio put the Portuguese side ahead at San Siro in the 16th minute and Jakub Kaminski added a second early in the second half.Bayer Leverkusen, finalists in 2024, began their Europa League campaign with a 2-0 win against the Slovenian champions Celje while Lyon were 2-1 winners at Anderlecht.The Cypriot championsOmonia Nicosiastunned the La Liga sideCelta Vigo1-0 while Rangers’ conquerorsJagiellonia Bialystokwere denied a point at the Greek giantsOlympiacosby Roman Yaremchuk’s late winner.Sparta PraguethrashedArarat-Armenia4-1 whileSturm GrazagainstRennesandHapoel Be’er ShevaversusDinamo Zagrebboth ended goalless.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Smit and his teammates issued plenty of reminders that AZ are more than merely deft in possession, but Le Bris’s starting XI was hardly shabby either and, after Wilson Isidor conjured a glorious chance, Le Fée’s shot hit the post.It was not long before another shot, from Hume this time, whizzed just wide of an upright. When, back in January 2022, Hume joined Sunderland, they were still in League One.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBack in the present Le Bris’s team ended the first half thoroughly dominant yet frustrated. The manager later blamed “overthinking”. Oufkir, meanwhile, was arguably fortunate to collect only a yellow card after sliding in recklessly on Le Fée and was replaced by Weslley Patati at the interval.AZ re-emerged for the second half invigorated and, as Smit wrong‑footed Sunderland’s rearguard before curling a shot inches wide, it was easy to see why he has collected so many admirers across Europe.View image in fullscreenLe Fée fires home the decisive penalty.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersPerhaps anxious not to be upstaged, Le Fée swiftly regained the limelight courtesy of a stellar pass that Isidor could not quite polish off.When Hume subsequently missed another presentable chance it seemed that De Busser’s goal must be protected by some sort of magnetic forcefield.Then Patati felled Le Fée in the area as he shaped to shoot and a player being scrutinised by the France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, stepped up to the spot.Having seen a penalty against Arsenal saved expertly by David Raya last Saturday, Le Fée looked a little nervous but he sent De Busser the wrong way as he struck a textbook kick low into the bottom corner. “It was important to score,” Le Bris said. “But Enzo stepped up with bravery and courage. He’s resilient.”Although Nordi Mukiele and Brian Brobbey, on as a substitute, should really have doubled the lead before Patati’s volley almost provided a late equaliser for AZ, that penalty proved just enough to launch Sunderland’s galleon on European waters.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueSunderlandAZ AlkmaarEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Raphinha cashes in against Santander with hat-trick as Barça hit seven | La Liga | The Guardian
description: João Cancelo (twice), Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored in Barcelona’s 7-2 rout of Racing Santander at Camp Nou
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: João Cancelo (twice), Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored in Barcelona’s 7-2 rout of Racing Santander at Camp Nou
Content: Raphinha shows three fingers to the crowd after completing his hat-trick against Racing Santander.Photograph: Alejandro García/EPAView image in fullscreenRaphinha shows three fingers to the crowd after completing his hat-trick against Racing Santander.Photograph: Alejandro García/EPALa LigaRaphinha cashes in against Santander with hat-trick as Barça hit sevenCancelo, Jesus and Lamine Yamal also score in routAtlético Madrid thrash Osasuna 4-0 to move into thirdAgence France-PresseWed 16 Sep 2026 18.10 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 19.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRaphinha scored a hat-trick asBarcelonarippedRacing Santanderto shreds in a spectacular 7-2 triumph in La Liga on Wednesday. The win makes Hansi Flick the club’s first manager to win ⁠the opening seven competitive matches of a season.João Cancelo, Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored for the unstoppable Catalan giants, who have netted 33 goals in those seven games across all competitions, and who moved three points clear of Real Madrid at the top ofLa Liga.With lightning flashing above the Camp Nou, Barça started at rapid pace and took the lead with a thunderbolt from Cancelo. The defender crashed a shot in off the crossbar from long range in the eighth minute.View image in fullscreenLamine Yamal celebrates scoring Barcelona’s seventh goal.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersDani Olmo twice came close before Raphinha won and converted a penalty for Barça’s second. The Brazilian was clumsily brought down by Pedro Felipe and thrashed the spot-kick into the bottom right corner.Santander pulled one back when Maguette Gueye barged his way through and produced a neat finish to beat Joan García in goal. However, it proved only brief respite, with Cancelo provoking the third with another long-range effort which deflected in off Asier Villalibre.Raphinha, thriving playing as a centre-forward, bagged Barça’s fourth after he was played in on goal by Olmo. Lamine Yamal should have added a fifth after the electric Karim Adeyemi was brought down in the box, but Julen Agirrezabala saved his penalty.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFootball Daily | Madrid endure an awkward night after T-shirt trouble and Elche scareRead moreBarça’s reserve goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny replaced García at half-time after the Spain international appeared to hurt himself while slipping as he went to get the ball. Lamine Yamal hit a post and later had a goal ruled out for offside, as the youngster suffered a more frustrating night than some of his colleagues.In the second half Yassir Zabiri pulled another back for Santander after a dreadful error from Szczesny, who tried and failed to dribble the ball. Zabiri tackled him to score.Barcelona’s fifth arrived almost immediately with another penalty after Adeyemi was brought down. Raphinha completed his hat-trick from the spot for his ninth league goal, extending his lead as the league’s top goalscorer.He was replaced by his compatriot Gabriel Jesus, who added the sixth with a sharp finish into the top corner after being played in by Lamine Yamal. The winger eventually got his goal when Adeyemi roared down the left wing and set him up for Barça’s seventh and final goal.Atlético Madridwarmed up for Saturday’s derby with Real with a 4-0 home win overOsasuna. Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Robin Le Normand and Alex Baena were on target in a one-sided contest at the Metropolitano as Diego Simeone’s side moved into third, five points behind Barcelona.Explore more on these topicsLa LigaBarcelonaRacing SantanderAtlético MadridOsasunaEuropean club footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Madrid endure an awkward night after T-shirt trouble and Elche scare | Soccer | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: Real Madrid become embroiled in controversy over Ceuta shirts and are then given an almighty scare by La Liga minnows
Author: Barry Glendenning
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: Real Madrid become embroiled in controversy over Ceuta shirts and are then given an almighty scare by La Liga minnows
Content: Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé looking like they would rather be elsewhere.Photograph: Jose Breton/NurPhoto/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenVinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé looking like they would rather be elsewhere.Photograph: Jose Breton/NurPhoto/ShutterstockFootball Daily newsletterSoccerMadrid endure an awkward night after T-shirt trouble and Elche scareSign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Barry GlendenningWed 16 Sep 2026 10.39 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 11.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleREAL UNEASEAnxious to sample some traditional Spanish culture while taking in a La Liga match years ago, Football Daily and some friends decamped to Gran Alicant. As we prepared to leave a quaint bodega (the Dick Turpin), where we’d been sampling the local hooch (Guinness), to travel to the nearby stadium, an elderly local resident with an unmistakable mackem accent informed us that the Elche home game to which we were heading was not being played until the following evening. It had fallen victim to Spanish TV’s infuriating habit of rescheduling random top-flight matches with little or no notice or consideration for Johnny-come-latelys who might have travelled from afar to watch them. We never did get to see Elche play in the flesh but did get to watch the current La Liga basement-dwellers give José Mourinho an almighty fright on TV on Tuesday night, as they wentthisclose to snatching a point fromReal Madrid.Allowed to spend 14 times more on players and coaching staff than their hosts at the Estadio Martínez Valero underLa Ligarules, it was no surprise to see Real Madrid go 2-0 up as they appeared to be cruising towards a routine rout of their lowly opposition. However, a succession of missed chances (hello, Vinícius Júnior) followed by second-half sucker punches from Abiel Osorio and Fer Niño meant Mourinho was sweating as Elche approached the final seven minutes on the front foot, looking for an unlikely winner. Sadly, there was no fairytale and Carlos Espí popped up with a late, late winner to break Elche hearts and dig his side out of one of several holes they have already found themselves in this season. While a balmy Tuesday night in Elche may not be the most glamorous of environments, not for the first, second, third, fourth or even 534th time in their history, Madrid found a way.“Three points and nothing more,” harrumphed Mourinho in his post-match interview. “The problem seems obvious to me. It’s harder to know why but it’s easier to understand that there are matches that seem over but in the end, aren’t. Matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them but don’t. After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease to losing control. With the changes I made in the end, I took all the risks. We won but I could have lost.” Modest to a T, as ever, Mourinho will be hoping for a better performance from his team when they make the short trip to the Wanda Metropolitano to face their city rivals Atlético on Sunday (or Saturday, depending on the whims of broadcasters) before the international break.While the out-of-sorts Vinícius Jr did little on Tuesday night beyond convince Arsenal fans they may have dodged a very expensive summer bullet, he was one of three Madrid stars who refused to show off T-shirts showing solidarity with the people of Ceuta that were handed to both sets of players as they made their way out on to the pitch before kick-off. Along with Kylian Mbappé and Ibrahima Konaté, Vinícius Jr chose not to show the slogan “Todos somos caballas” (“We are all mackerels”), in support of the Spanish exclave which was overwhelmed by the arrival of 80,000 migrants, mostly from Morocco, in recent months. Subsequently lambasted in some quarters for being too supportive of the migrants and not supportive enough of the citizens of Ceuta, it was an awkward situation where the Madrid players were put on the spot and simply couldn’t do right for doing wrong.LIVE ON BIG WEBSITEJoin Niall McVeigh at 8pm (BST) for a red-hot Bigger Vase clockwatch, while Will Unwin will be on deck at the same time for Rumblews Cup goal updates.QUOTE OF THE DAY“I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, ‘I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever’. That was the feeling. That was the moment” – as part of the FA’s forthcoming feature ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’, Thomas Tuchel was recently interviewed by Daniel Sturridge about the aftermath ofEngland’s famous 3-2 win over Mexicoat the Azteca, and made a bizarre admission about his eating habits while showing an alarming misunderstanding of the body’s digestive system.View image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel failed to mention what he was chewing during that second half with Argentina.Photograph: Ricardo Mazalán/APFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markI almost wish I was a West Ham fan. As an eternally suffering Spurs supporter, I find myself looking enviously towards the London Stadium these days. The Hammers are top of the table, banging in goal after goal (already 20 more than Spurs’ tally in the league). They score even when they lose and seem to have bought a proper No 9. My Spurs, meanwhile, continue the tradition of the last two years in style, sitting comfortably in 17th with 1,047 wingers on contract, and getting knocked out of one of the competitions they could ‘conceivably’ have won, the only competition they seem to be able to score goals in as well. In hindsight, West Ham made the right choice to go down. Hammers fans, you are welcome!” – Yannick Woudstra (and no others).double quotation markHugh Fordham’s idea [Tuesday’s Football Daily letters] has some merit. But it reminded me of a pithy comment by Bill Nicholson. ‘Do you think he was interfering with play?’, he was asked. Nicholson responded: “If he’s not interfering with play, what’s he doing on the pitch?!’” – Harry McDonald.double quotation markIn support of Hugh Fordham’s suggestion, I remember discussing the idea of interfering with play while on a training course for referees back in the 1960s. We were told that unless someone was ‘lying injured near the corner flag’ any player should be treated as being involved in play. Not a lot of room for subjectivity in those days. And obviously no thought of stopping play for the hypothetical injured player!” – Trevor Field.If you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to …Harry McDonald. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, arehere.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version,just visit this page and follow the instructions.Explore more on these topicsFootballFootball Daily newsletterReal MadridLa LiganewslettersShareReuse this content

title: ‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine Yamal  | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Mikel Merino says Max Dowman reminds him of Lamine Yamal after the Arsenal prodigy continued his development by scoring twice in his side’s 4-2 win over Ipswich
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Mikel Merino says Max Dowman reminds him of Lamine Yamal after the Arsenal prodigy continued his development by scoring twice in his side’s 4-2 win over Ipswich
Content: Max Dowman celebrates scoring his second goal for Arsenal in their Carabao Cup victory against Ipswich.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAView image in fullscreenMax Dowman celebrates scoring his second goal for Arsenal in their Carabao Cup victory against Ipswich.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAArsenal‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine YamalTeenager continues development with two goals at IpswichMerino: ‘He is a big talent and we have to take care of him’Jacob SteinbergWed 16 Sep 2026 12.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 16.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Merino says Max Dowman reminds him of Lamine Yamal after the Arsenal prodigy continued his development by scoring twice in his side’s4-2 win against Ipswich.Dowman, who has been given a host of opportunities at senior level by Mikel Arteta, starred after being handed his first appearance of the season, at Portman Road on Tuesday. The 16-year-old attacker’s classy double easedArsenalinto the last 16 of the Carabao Cup and left Arteta admitting that containing the hype around the England youth international is not an easy task.Arsenal are managing Dowman carefully and Merino is well placed to see how young talents can benefit from listening to managers and older players. The Arsenal midfielder plays with Lamine Yamal for Spain and believes Dowman is as fearless as the 19-year-old winger.Lewis Koumas on playing ‘the Liverpool way’, showing hunger and hopes for the futureRead more“There are some similarities in terms of their character,” he said. “They don’t care about the spotlight. They thrive when pressure is at the highest. They are always up for the challenge and they are not shy at all – even facing the biggest names in the game.”Merino, who also scored against Ipswich, raved about Dowman. “He is an unbelievable talent. We knew it, but every time he goes on the pitch and plays against grown men he makes the difference. He is a big talent and we have to take care of him.“We have to keep pushing him. He needs to keep learning – eyes and ears open always. There is still big room for improvement in a lot of areas and he knows that. So we are going to be by his side trying to get him to his best level.“It is a thin line. It is very difficult to have equilibrium sometimes with him, because obviously you want him to shine and show everyone the talent that he has. But you have to sometimes remind them that they are human beings and they are part of a bigger squad and team.“The good thing with these kind of players – Lamine and Max – is that they are special talents, but at the same time they are very humble. They are always keen to learn and listen to the veterans. That is priceless.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMerino also praised Marli Salmon after the 17-year-old impressed against Ipswich. “In that position as a centre-back, you need to be very mature,” he said.“It’s very important you don’t make many mistakes. Every action is crucial. It’s the same as with Max, he is an unbelievable talent. We try to teach them our experience and they are very good at listening.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘We can’t accept that’: Carrick urges Manchester United to respond after cup collapse | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: The Manchester United manager said after the 3-2 defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup: ‘I take responsibility … it doesn’t feel good at the moment’
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The Manchester United manager said after the 3-2 defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup: ‘I take responsibility … it doesn’t feel good at the moment’
Content: Michael Carrick said Manchester United ‘have to go back to winning football matches’ after defeat by Brighton.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick said Manchester United ‘have to go back to winning football matches’ after defeat by Brighton.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester United‘We can’t accept that’: Carrick urges Manchester United to respond after cup collapse‘I take responsibility … it doesn’t feel good at the moment’United beaten 3-2 by Brighton after taking two-goal leadJamie Jacksonat Old TraffordWed 16 Sep 2026 18.49 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick admitted Manchester United’sCarabao Cup capitulation against Brightonthat was greeted by boos at Old Trafford was unacceptable and that answers had to be found at Fulham on Sunday.United were knocked out 3-2 by Fabian Hürzeler’s visitors after leading 2-0 after 10 minutes through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount. Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas in first‑half added time, Pascal Gross on 65 minutes and Maxim De Cuyper four minutes later eliminated United.De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comebackRead moreIt was the first time United had lost after leading 2-0 at Old Trafford for 50 years and the first time since 1984 they had been defeated there after being ahead at half-time.Carrick’s side have beaten onlyIpswich in the leagueandSabah in the Champions League. “Under pressure? That doesn’t bother me one bit,” he said.“I understand what goes on and how the world works. What bothers me is winning games and I believe we will do, but we have to do it pretty quickly. We can’t accept that [the manner of the defeat] as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that’s on me. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. It doesn’t feel good at the moment.”Carrick said of the boos at the end: “I totally understand the feelings of the supporters.”The manager was asked about JJ Gabriel, the 15-year-old academy player who has informed Unitedhe wants to leave. “We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He’s a 15-year-old boy. It’s more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really,” Carrick said. “He’s certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHürzeler, who made six changes, was delighted with the win. “I am not sure how many players on the pitch had experienced winning here, we have a lot of newcomers but when we play to our level we can compete with anyone in the league,” the Brighton manager said. In the next round his side will travel to the winner of the game on Thursday between Manchester City and Norwich. “We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickBrighton & Hove AlbionCarabao CupnewsShareReuse this content

title: Points deduction puts Leicestershire on brink as Warwickshire go top: County Championship cricket, day two – as it happened | County Championship | The Guardian
description: It was advantage Warwickshire at the top but the most significant action came off the pitch, with Leicestershire all but relegated after a points deduction
Author: Tanya Aldred
Headline: It was advantage Warwickshire at the top but the most significant action came off the pitch, with Leicestershire all but relegated after a points deduction
Content: 6h ago15.52 EDTRoundup: Warwickshire win but points deduction puts Leicestershire on brinkIt was advantageWarwickshireat the top but perhaps the most significant action of the day came off the pitch and at the bottom, withLeicestershireall but relegated after a points deduction.TheCricketRegulator had charged Leicestershire after the Grace Road pitch was rated as poor for last month’s win against Glamorgan. The cricket discipline panel has upheld the charge, leading to the deduction of the 19 points picked up for the victory plus eight more as a penalty. A Leicestershire statement said “the club is reviewing its position and considering all available options”, but the deduction left them bottom of the table, 38 points adrift of the last safe spot. WithHampshire225 ahead with seven wickets standing, Leicestershire’s hopes in what is now a must-win match are slim.Warwickshire flourish a 19-point hand on the table and wait after a second two-day victory in succession.Essex, further weakened by overnight substitutions to Shane Snater and Tom Westley, gave them the upper hand by conceding another 40 runs for the last wicket, thanks largely to an unbeaten 88 from Sam Hain. The Indian spinner Manav Suthar, with five for 75, and Chris Woakes, with three for 33, were too hot for Essex and Warwickshire easily knocked off the 133 needed.The morning bell at Chelmsford was rung by the BBC’s Dick Davies, retiring after 31 years covering Essex cricket. Up at Headingley, Craig Overton continued his one-man attempt to haulSomersetover the line. His 64 not out, full of humpty and grace, rescued his team from the doldrums of 86 for eight, in companionship with Migael Pretorius, who found his long-lost batting form with a free-flowing 58.Overton was last man out to Ben Cliff’s, whose astonishing eight for 76 were the best bowling figures for a Yorkshireman at Headingley since Graham Stevenson’s eight for 57 in 1980. He led Yorkshire off grinning, applauding teammates behind.Overton soon spoiled their fun, nobbling Will Luxton’s middle stump with his second ball, and removing Adam Lyth a couple of overs later. Jonny Bairstow came and went to a Nureyev catch at cover by Archie Vaughan but George Hill and Dom Bess stopped the rot with an unbroken seventh-wicket stand of 74 as spectators in the East Stand enjoyed some afternoon sun to stretch Yorkshire’s lead to 139.At Hove,Nottinghamshirewere held up by an obdurateSussex, who picked up the only Division One batting point of the round thanks to half centuries for Tom Clark, Charlie Tear and Tom Price.Kentneed 56 to beatLancashireand get their promotion points on the board. Zak Crawley (84) and Matt Milnes (40 not out) ushered Kent to a first-innings lead of 53, before Milnes had a go with the ball and helped chisel Lancashire out for 192. Sam Northeast and Tawanda Muyeye took Kent towards a good night’s sleep.Asa Tribe’s first hundred of the season, on a wicket where 20 wickets had fallen the day before, eased Glamorgan’s relegation nerves, even before the Leicestershire news.Share

title: Matt Fitzpatrick casts doubt on Dubai title defence over fears about conflict | European Tour | The Guardian
description: The world No 4 said he was ‘not comfortable’ appearing at the DP World Tour’s season-closing events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai amid the Middle East conflict
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: The world No 4 said he was ‘not comfortable’ appearing at the DP World Tour’s season-closing events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai amid the Middle East conflict
Content: Matt Fitzpatrick says he would be wary of travelling to the Middle East after having a child in August.Photograph: Colin Hubbard/APView image in fullscreenMatt Fitzpatrick says he would be wary of travelling to the Middle East after having a child in August.Photograph: Colin Hubbard/APEuropean TourMatt Fitzpatrick casts doubt on Dubai title defence over fears about conflictWorld No 4 may snub World Tour Championship‘I’m not comfortable playing in the Middle East’Ewan Murrayat WentworthWed 16 Sep 2026 11.01 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMatt Fitzpatrick, the world No 4, has admitted to reservations over appearing at the DP World Tour’s end‑of‑season events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai because of the conflict in the Middle East.The Englishman, who is due to defend the DP World Tour Championship title in Dubai, has accused the tour of being “very vague” over plans to retain or move the tournaments. In Fitzpatrick’s mind, it is a “no-brainer” to play elsewhere, but he believes his sentiment will not feature strongly in the thoughts of the tour’s hierarchy.Fitzpatrick even suggested that Formula One is reconsidering staging the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in December after races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were called off this year because of the Iran war, though itremains on the calendar.Top golfers to get no favours for PGA Tour return after LIV bankruptcyRead moreThe Abu Dhabi Championship is due to take place from 5 November, with the DP World Tour Championship slated for the following week. Every indication is that those competitions will happen in the United Arab Emirates, despite contingencies involving Turkey, Spain and Portugal known to have been considered.“As things stand right now, I would say I’m not that comfortable,” Fitzpatrick said about playing in the Middle East. “A few things have changed for me. I had a child in August and that changes things a bit more.“It would feel a little bit weird, given what I’m reading elsewhere. Things can change overnight, I’m sure. I think it seems to be going down that path of things are getting better. I’ve looked on the UK [government] website, I know they changed it from essential travel only to one step better than that.“I know the tour has been on this for a long time. It’s frustrating the decision hasn’t been made so you can plan. But I understand there’s a lot of moving parts to that and it’s difficult to make these decisions.“If the tour do go, I’m sure they have had the best advice possible on what that looks like. As things stand, I wouldn’t necessarily be too keen on going. I know there’s been discussions on what Formula One is doing. I’ve heard they might not be going there, so it begs the question, would we, I guess.”Fitzpatrick later made reference to missile strike damage to a hotel in Dubai where he had dinner in the week of his 2025 win at JumeirahGolfEstates. “That’s very scary,” he said.” Pressed on whether he felt his viewpoint would be heeded, Fitzpatrick said: “I don’t think so.”Fitzpatrick said his management was informed in April that the tour would make a decision by June. “I’m sure the Middle East want the DP World Tour to go there badly because it’s a great event for two weeks. It’s great for tourism and all that sort of stuff with it, but I wouldn’t say that I have had regular contact.“It’s been very vague the whole time and they have not necessarily kind of had open communication.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMatt Fitzpatrick is due to defend the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty ImagesThe topic is a rising one for discussion this week at the PGA Championship, the DP World Tour’s flagship competition, at Wentworth. A spokesperson for the DP World Tour said: “We are in constant dialogue with our members and their management teams about the tournaments they play in but ultimately players’ individual schedule choices are a matter for them to decide.“As far as our playoffs are concerned, it remains our intention to play as scheduled in the UAE, but we continue to monitor the situation and take advice from our international travel advisers.”Should Fitzpatrick and others opt to skip UAE-based tournaments, it would clearly undermine their status. Rory McIlroy is seeking to win a record-equalling eighth European order of merit – now the Race to Dubai – title.The Open champion, Ryan Fox, is content to be guided by the tour. “There are some concerns,” the New Zealander said. “I’m of the opinion that the tour is doing their due diligence. If they feel like it’s safe for us to go, I’m willing to support that.“But I can understand, also, why guys have some reservations. I’ll keep monitoring it. If I feel like it’s not the right decision, I might not go, but at this point I trust the tour’s decision in that regard.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean TourGolfnewsShareReuse this content

title: USA exit U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism | USA women's football team | The Guardian
description: An exit at the hands of Brazil continues the Americans’ difficult run of form at youth events
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: An exit at the hands of Brazil continues the Americans’ difficult run of form at youth events
Content: Kennedy Fuller led the US with three goals at this month’s U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/FIFA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKennedy Fuller led the US with three goals at this month’s U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/FIFA/Getty ImagesUSA women's football teamUSA exit U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticismBrazil advance to quarter-finals in PolandAmericans have not won tournament since 2012US youth teams have struggled in recent showingsJeff RueterWed 16 Sep 2026 13.14 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 15.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Brazil goalkeeper Thaís Lima made a crucial save on Emeri Adames’s attempt to begin the shootout, opening the eventual 5-4 finish in Katowice, Poland.The result extends a difficult run of form for US youth national teams across the men’s and women’s programs. This is the third time since last October that a US youth team have failed to win a knockout game at a World Cup: the U-17 boys and the U-17 girls both exited in the last 16 of their respective tournaments in shootouts. The U-20 men fell in the quarter-final of their World Cup in October 2025.The US, holders of 2024 Olympic gold in women’s soccer and winners of two of the past three senior Women’s World Cups, last won the U-20 tournament in 2012, with a squad headlined by Crystal Dunn, Julie (Johnston) Ertz and Sam Mewis, all of whom are now retired.From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World CupRead moreIn Poland, the Americans struggled to advance from their group, losing the opener against Italy before playing Japan to a 2-2 draw. A 9-0 rout of New Zealand was enough to reach the knockout round as one of the tournament’s top third-place sides. Brazil comfortably finished atop their group, beating Tanzania, Canada and England by a 9-2 aggregate.While far from as testy asthe senior national teams’ friendlies in June, the US and Brazil played a fairly scrappy game Wednesday. Brazil defender Sofia opened the scoring from a 59th-minute corner kick, while Seattle Reign midfielder Ainsley McCammon equalized from the run of play late in the 63rd. Neither team was able to find a breakthrough in the ensuing hour, leading to Lima’s heroics to open the shootout.This is Brazil’s third straight quarter-final appearance at a U-20 Women’s World Cup, and seventh in 12 appearances. Their joint best finish was a pair of third-place showings in 2006 and 2022.Emma Hayes ‘worried’ about tournament’s calendarThe timing of this year’s U-20 Women’s World Cup has drawn scrutiny from ex-players and coaches. Staged every other year, the tournament usually falls in either August or September, with this installment falling on the later end of the general timeframe. It is not being held in a Fifa window, so many in-season club teams opted not to release their players.On Tuesday, a group of current and former players including Alex Morgan, Marta, Dunn and Sophia Wilson signedan open letterasking Fifa to reconsider the scheduling of its U-20 Women’s World Cups. Emma Hayes told ESPN that she was concerned about the mettle of US youth national teams, which have historically struggled in major tournaments and World Cups given the federation’s past approach to youth development that deprioritized competitions.“When I speak about this subject, I am sending a warning sign that I am worried,” Hayes told ESPN. “I am massively worried about the direction for and the lack of all of those experiences for American players.”A September tournament is complicated for players already signed to clubs regardless of how their league operates. For players in fall-to-spring seasons, like the Women’s Super League, it picks off young players fresh from club preseason, hampering their ability to work into the first team and overlapping with the start of their seasons. For other leagues on spring-to-fall timelines, like the NWSL, clubs are put in the position to accept or reject call-ups during an important point of the regular season.Age-eligible US players who were absent from this tournament squad include OL Lyonnes midfielder Lily Yohannes, Bay midfielder Claire Hutton, rising center-back Jordyn Bugg and playmaking technician Melanie Barcenas.North Korea are the defending champions of the tournament, which ends with the 27 September final.Explore more on these topicsUSA women's football teamWomen's footballUS sportsEmma HayesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Watching Cavan Sullivan, excitement is tempered by memories of hypetrains past | MLS | The Guardian
description: The 16-year-old Union star isn’t the first wunderkind to be feted by the American soccersphere
Author: Leander Schaerlaeckens
Headline: The 16-year-old Union star isn’t the first wunderkind to be feted by the American soccersphere
Content: Cavan Sullivan made his Union debut as a 14-year-old in 2024.Photograph: Isaiah Vazquez/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCavan Sullivan made his Union debut as a 14-year-old in 2024.Photograph: Isaiah Vazquez/Getty ImagesMLSWatching Cavan Sullivan, excitement is tempered by memories of hypetrains pastLeander SchaerlaeckensThe 16-year-old Union star isn’t the first wunderkind to be feted by the American soccersphereWed 16 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 07.01 EDTShareThe trouble with trying not to hype up Cavan Sullivan is that he keeps on doing cool stuff. Like this past weekend, when he scampers along on aPhiladelphia Unionbreakaway, loses his man by stopping so suddenly it’s as if he’s pulled a ripcord, back-heels the cutback behind his standing leg, watches it slowly kiss off the far post and in, and celebrated the goal by bowing and doffing an imaginary top hat to the crowd.Like when he doubles the score by setting up an attack and finishing it himself with a left-footed lash through the goalkeeper’s legs form an acute angle. Like when he fashions yetanothergoal by holding up the play and then suddenly springs a teammate up the right flank.And that’s just this past weekend.It’s hard not to get worked up when an American, two weeks and a day before his 17th birthday, almost matches Lionel Messi for goal involvements in Major League Soccer and the Leagues Cup since the World Cup. When he powers an entire team of grown men to a 10-game unbeaten run. When he breaks Freddy Adu’s record as the youngest Major League Soccer debutant by 13 days, at 14 years and 293 days old. When he has netted six goals and five assists in his last eight matches. When he appears to be on the eve of his first United States men’s national team call-up.When his swagger and flair arevindicated by the advanced metrics,which suggestthat he has already compiled the best MLS season ever by a teenager, outdoing Alphonso Davies. That he is,in fact, the league’s second-best American player right now.What makes Cavan Sullivan so tantalizing is that he isn’t theoretical.And yet we wince.We have been down this road before.That way madness lies, let me shun that– so warned King Lear.As an American soccer community, we have developed a reflexive recoil against the Godding up of yet another prodigy. Still, it’s hard to resist, even though we know better. From the experience of Bobby Convey, and Jamar Beasley, and John O’Brien, and Jozy Altidore, and Juan Agudelo, and Brek Shea, and Julian Green, and Gedion Zelalem. They had skills and bodies and brains we could dream on, which we never managed to resist.Why David Beckham will have my vote for the US Soccer Hall of Fame | Pablo Iglesias MaurerRead moreDid you even remember Green and Zelalem? Green is 31 and presently without a club; Zelalem, now 29, plays for New Mexico United. Both were promised to us as potentially first American male superstar when they emerged from the Bayern Munich and Arsenal academies, respectively. But then, all the men on that list, and so many more, were supposed to be that. None of them were.We’ve been doing this since the 1970s, when it was decided that Kyle Rote Jr, son of the gridiron football hero, would put soccer on the map. He did indeed become famous, but much less for what he did on a soccer field than for thrice winning the popular gameshow Superstars – wherein top players from different sports competed in a series of athletic events. He led the North American Soccer League in scoring as a rookie and then tailed off, taking a “sabbatical” to lead a hunger relief mission to Cambodia in 1980 and never playing soccer again.They weren’t all failures. Several had solid professional careers. Altidore had a highly productive spell on the United States men’s national team – he is still its third all-time leading scorer, behind Landon Donovan and Clint Dempsey. His club resume, however, amounts to two good seasons in the Netherlands and half a dozen strong campaigns in Major League Soccer, after he had been discarded by five different European clubs.There’s still no telling, exactly, what the now-23-year-old Gio Reyna might or might not become. His body hasn’t cooperated, breaking down again and again, and neither has he managed to muster the consistency to become a regular and productive starter on a European club (that may change this season with Strasbourg). He’s bounced around, largely anonymously, briefly resurfacing for World Cups. It feels like a long time ago now, when he was 17 and fit seamlessly into Borussia Dortmund’s attacking diamond with Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going upRead moreOf all the chosen ones, only Christian Pulisic has really panned out something like we had hoped. He has, however, never really been the focal point in the attack of any of his three European clubs. And he’s developed an odd penchant for falling out of favor after two or three seasons, tumbling down the depth chart at Dortmund and then Chelsea and now Milan. Under new manager Ruben Amorim, Pulisic, the author of 52 goals and assists over the last three Serie A campaigns – albeit notably fewer of them in the 2025-26 season – has been benched and has appeared just once in the Italian league.And all of them toiled under the looming specter of Adu. More than two decades on from Freddymania, his name is still invoked as a cautionary tale. He works as a personal skills coach now, and has done since last playing professionally five years ago.So we proceed carefully, taking great pains not to make the same mistakes again.The thing is, Sullivan has already scored more goals in two-thirds of an MLS campaign than Adu did in his highest-scoring season, his rookie year with DC United in 2004. And the league is a hell of a lot harder to score in these days. It’sbetter set upto handle transcendent talent, too.Unlike most of the others, there are real numbers there. Real performances. Real highlight clips, captured at the senior level against credible opposition. Manchester City certainly think he’s real, long ago arranging for his transfer when he turns 18. It’s all there, other than the size of Sullivan himself. That may prove problematic. But then he wouldn’t be the first undersized superstar.And yet.Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts,which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.Explore more on these topicsMLSUS sportsPhiladelphia UnioncommentShareReuse this content

title: ‘Godfather of AI’ says tech regulation is nearing Covid-style pivot moment | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: Safety crisis makes it more likely that governments will be spurred into action, says Yoshua Bengio
Author: Dan Milmo
Headline: Safety crisis makes it more likely that governments will be spurred into action, says Yoshua Bengio
Content: Bengio is a prominent voice in the campaign to rein in breakneck AI development.Photograph: Atlantic StudiosView image in fullscreenBengio is a prominent voice in the campaign to rein in breakneck AI development.Photograph: Atlantic StudiosAI (artificial intelligence)‘Godfather of AI’ says tech regulation is nearing Covid-style pivot momentSafety crisis makes it more likely that governments will be spurred into action, says Yoshua BengioDan MilmoGlobal technology editorWed 16 Sep 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 15.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleConcerns over AI safety are reaching a point where governments realise they must act to protect the public, similarly to in the Covid pandemic, according to one of the “godfathers” of the technology.Yoshua Bengio said recent events, including a “swarm” of OpenAI agentshacking a startupandtech insider warnings of an existential threat, were cutting through – making government action more likely.The Canadian computer scientist, a prominent voice in the campaign to rein in breakneck AI development, said he was now “more optimistic than many observers because I see the public moving”.Comparing the AI safety crisis to the onset of the Covid pandemic in 2020, Bengio said: “Think about how quickly governments moved after the beginning of the pandemic when they realised that public safety, their future, democracy, was in danger. You would expect that they move quickly. So we are, I think, nearing that point.”Concern over the potential threat of powerful AI systems has reached a new pitch in recent months after a series of safety incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic agents carrying out unsanctioned activities such as hacking third parties, hijacking a German website, and using fake identities to try to trick developers.His comments came as 42 fellows and foreign members of the Royal Society wrote to the organisation’s president, Sir Paul Nurse, to express their “extreme concern” over the pace of AI development. “By the time the situation becomes obvious to the wider public, it may be too late to act,” the researchers wrote in an open letter to Nurse. “We believe this is an emergency, and call on the Royal Society to use its influence to convey this view to government and the media.”Last week, a researcher at Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude chatbot, resigned after warning that colleagues believed AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade”. Days later, Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei,called for a slowdownin the pace of cutting-edge AI development – a move that was immediately supported by OpenAI, Google and Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX.However, sceptics of the “slowdown” call have claimed that calls by major AI firms are an example of “regulatory capture”, where companies persuade governments to introduce safety regimes that raise the cost of smaller rivals being able to compete. They also claim existential fears overshadow more immediate issues with AI such as its impact oncopyright-protected workand human rights.Bengio said he disagreed with the regulatory capture argument because a slowdown by leading AI firms would “cost them financially”. The US president, Donald Trump, has rejected a slowdown, saying he does not want the US to lose its lead over China in the AI race.View image in fullscreenYoshua Bengio, a professor at the University of Montreal, won a Turing award in 2018.Photograph: Andrej Ivanov/AFP/Getty ImagesBengio spoke as the Canadian and German governments announced funding of up to C$300m (£160m) for hisnon-profit organisationdedicated to creating an “honest AI” that will act as a guardrail against rogue agents – AI tools that carry out sequences of tasks without human intervention.Bengio, a professor at the University of Montreal, earned the “godfather of AI” moniker after winning the 2018 Turing award, seen as the equivalent of a Nobel prize for computing. He shared it with Geoffrey Hinton,who later won a Nobel, and Yann LeCun, the former chief AI scientist at Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta.Bengio’s organisation, LawZero, is developing a system called Scientist AI that will act as a guardrail against AI agents showing deceptive or self-preserving behaviour, such as trying to avoid being turned off. LawZero is also funded by the Gates Foundation, the chipmaker Nvidia, and Coefficient Giving, a philanthropic body linked to effective altruism, a movement that believes AI poses an existential threat.The LawZero technology is viewed by Bengio as a counterpoint to reinforcement learning, a trial-and-error development technique used by major AI companies where AIs are rewarded for working out how to carry out a specific task. The Canadian computer scientist believes, along with other experts, this training technique encourages AIs to pursue their goals recklessly and cause harm in the process, as shown by the OpenAI “swarm”.Deployed alongside an AI agent, Bengio’s technology would raise potentially harmful behaviour by an autonomous system – having weighed whether its actions could cause harm. Bengio expects the technology to be deployed for other uses eventually, such as accelerating scientific breakthroughs.Explore more on these topicsAI (artificial intelligence)ComputingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Amazon to launch Ring ‘neighbourhood watch’ app in UK amid US privacy fears | Amazon | The Guardian
description: Doorbell firm aims to replace WhatsApp or Facebook groups with platform where people can post about safety or lost pets
Author: Samuel Gibbs
Headline: Doorbell firm aims to replace WhatsApp or Facebook groups with platform where people can post about safety or lost pets
Content: The Neighbours app will be available for free within the main Ring app from 21 October.Composite: RingView image in fullscreenThe Neighbours app will be available for free within the main Ring app from 21 October.Composite: RingAmazonAmazon to launch Ring ‘neighbourhood watch’ app in UK amid US privacy fearsDoorbell firm aims to replace WhatsApp or Facebook groups with platform where people can post about safety or lost petsSamuel GibbsConsumer technology editorWed 16 Sep 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAmazon’s doorbell camera maker Ring is to launch its Neighbours community app in the UK in an attempt to supplant neighbourhood WhatsApp or Facebook groups.The service is intended as a modern equivalent of a community message board, where neighbours can post about safety, community matters or lost pets.It is being made available free of charge inside the existing Ring app for UK users from 21 October and can be used by anyone, regardless of whether they own one of the brand’s products.Allowing AI firms to collude to ‘pace the frontier’ is a dangerous propositionRead more“We used to have the village noticeboard, but as things have changed we no longer have that local connection,” said Dave Ward, the managing director of international for Ring. “Instead what you see in WhatsApp or other services is quite a broad-stroked flood of information, the bins being left out, that sort of thing. It’s a big group that ends up getting muted.“We’re trying to tailor this down to just the things that really matter to your immediate community and then it becomes super useful.”Those who join the service set their address and a radius of between 0.1 and five miles to join the local community.Some of the more controversial features of the Neighbours service from the US will not be immediately available in the UK. That includes the Neighbours Verified service, which allows entities and services such as the local fire brigade to post advisory messages to local communities.The Community Requests feature, which allows the police to issue calls for footage from Ring cameras in a local area in response to incidents, has drawn the mostire from privacy campaigners. It allows those with footage of incidents to share it with the police on an opt-in and per-event basis. The police are not informed of those that choose not to share footage.Both features are being developed for release in the UK but not until later this year at the earliest.Neighbours will launch with basic anonymised posting narrowed into categories, which must conform to a strict set of guidelines barring illegal content, discrimination, speculation or multiple other conditions.View image in fullscreenRing’s Neighbours service aims to help owners find lost pets.Composite: RingThe posts are moderated by AI and humans before and after being published. Content can be shared from Ring doorbells and other cameras.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We are going to coach people to make sure they’re creating the right sort of post, asking them if that’s really something they want to write or whether it really need that descriptive term, to help stop the type of content no one wants to see and make it more community focused. That’s very different to other places [such as WhatsApp groups],” Ward said.Amazon bought the video doorbell and home security camera maker in 2018 in a deal reportedlyworth more than $1bn.The new service will also have a feature called “Search Party for Dogs”, which allows users of lost pets to post an image and report of a lost dog.Those in the neighbourhood who have Ring cameras and a suitable cloud subscription can opt in to join the search. They will then be notified if their cameras see a dog, prompted to check whether it is the correct dog, and then can optionally notify and share the video with the pet owner.In an attempt to negate some privacy fears, Ring recentlyannounced a new default encryption mechanismfor camera footage called TAKE (throw away the key encryption). This feature provides Ring’s systems time-limited keys to the recordings, blocking the company and others access to the videos after 24 hours. Further processing or access, including by law enforcement, requires user consent to issue replacement 24-hour keys from the user’s Ring app.Explore more on these topicsAmazonAppsTechnology sectorConsumer affairsnewsShareReuse this content

title: The US government is failing Americans on AI | Shakeel Hashim | The Guardian
description: Trump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safe
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Trump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safe
Content: Elon Musk, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenElon Musk, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman.Composite: Getty ImagesAI (artificial intelligence)The US government is failing Americans on AIShakeel HashimTrump and Republicans want companies to regulate themselves. It’s a dereliction of duty that will make AI less safeWed 16 Sep 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 06.03 EDTShareIt is hard to getSam Altman, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei to agree on much. But over the weekend, all three AI company CEOs called for AI development to slow down in the face of growing, alarming risks. Their employees are sounding the siren too, with one researcher publicly quitting and accusing OpenAI and Anthropic of “gambling with our lives”.The combination of dire warnings from insiders and growing real-world evidence of rogue AIs should, in a sane world, lead to government action. Instead,Donald Trumpand the Republican leadership have their heads in the sand.On Sunday, Trumpdismissedindustry concerns, accusing “very negative forces” of “raising exaggerated concerns”. House Speaker Mike Johnson,meanwhile, made it clear that Congress won’t be acting anytime soon.“They can self-police. They can self-regulate,” he said, never mind the fact that those pushing the frontier are the ones begging for legislation.Anthropic’s CEO calls for AI slowdown as Nvidia’s urges accelerationRead moreIn failing to act, the Trump administration and Republicans are failing the American people. The risks of AI are real: many of those developing the technology believe it is advancing far faster than their ability to control it or manage the risks.
